items.title: World reacts to Lula’s victory in Brazil’s presidential election
items.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has secured a fourth nonconsecutive term, defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a run-off . Bolsonaro, however, has called for Sunday’s vote to be annulled over an “unacceptable” two-hour voting extension granted by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, despite both candidates having requested additional voting time. The election results have drawn reactions across the world, with left-wing global figures celebrating Lula’s victory. Here’s how the world reacted: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Sheinbaum congratulated Lula in a post on X. “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won,” she wrote. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney In his congratulatory post, Carney credited Lula with advancing relations between Canada and Brazil. “Let us seize this opportunity to strengthen them further, together – to create new promising commercial prospects, protect the environment, and ensure greater prosperity for both our populations,” he wrote on X. US officials and politicians US President Donald Trump’s son Donald Trump Jr criticised the result, referring to the two-hour voting time extension. “If a conservative government in Brazil did this, everyone in the mainstream press in America would lose their minds, but I guess they’re just choosing to be silent because it’s all for the cause,” he said. Progressive Senator Bernie Sanders, meanwhile, congratulated Lula’s “extraordinary re-election victory”, saying the Brazilian president has “stood up” for workers and democracy and will continue to do so for the next four years. Congressman Ro Khanna said in a post on X: “People all across the world are fighting back against extremism. With Lula in Brazil, they just won. Authoritarian leaders always attack democracy because they stand no chance against the will of their people.” Khanna added that Trump “must respect the results and not undermine Brazil’s elections”. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote on X: “The people united will never be defeated!” California Governor Gavin Newsom’s media office released a statement, saying he is “proud to stand with Brazil and partners around the world who share our commitment to defending democracy, protecting our environment, strengthening workers’ rights, and building an economy that works for working families”. Chinese Foreign Ministry China congratulated Lula through a statement by Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun. “China has noted that Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court has announced President Lula has won the second round of the Brazilian general election, and expresses its congratulations,” Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing, adding that Beijing was “willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future.” Russian presidency The Kremlin says it welcomed the re-election of Lula da Silva and praised him for his contribution to bilateral ties and to the intergovernmental BRICS organisation. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Lula had done a lot for bilateral ties and for developing BRICS and hoped for more of the same. Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel Diaz-Canel said Lula’s “historic” win “ensures the continuity of the path of peace, sovereignty, and social justice embarked upon by the Brazilian people under your leader”. “Brazil can count on Cuba in the construction of the unity and integration of our Great Homeland, Latin American and Caribbean,” he wrote in a post on X. Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast Kast said he spoke on the phone with Lula to congratulate him on his victory. “Chile and Brazil have a lot of shared future ahead, and we will continue working on an agenda that strengthens relations between our countries in economic integration and the fight against organised crime in the region,” he said on X. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori In a congratulatory post on X, Fujimori reaffirmed Peru’s “willingness to strengthen our strategic alliance, integration, cooperation and the sustainable development of the Amazon that we share” with Brazil. Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz “Bolivia and Brazil are neighbouring and sister countries, united by a shared history and common challenges,” Rodrigo wrote on X. The two countries will continue to work together to strengthen ties and “generate more opportunities for our nations”, he added. Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino “I congratulate the ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Brazilian ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌people for this democratic day and especially President Lula for the victory!” Mulino wrote on X. “We will continue working together for our countries.” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen Von der Leyen congratulated Lula on X, proclaiming that democracy and multilateralism “have won” in Brazil. “Europe’s partnership with Brazil is thriving. We will remain by your side for the years to come,” she added. “Together we will keep working closely for free and open trade. A rules-based global order. And strong ambitions for our climate.” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez Sanchez hailed the victory of his leftist Brazilian ally as a “progressive comeback”. “A great victory for Lula! What has happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The global progressive comeback has just begun,” Sanchez posted on X, after Lula’s recovery from a first round loss halted a string of right-wing gains in Latin America. French President Emmanuel Macron Macron called for efforts to “strengthen our strategic partnership” after Lula’s win. “France and Brazil have much to build together,” Macron said on X, saying their two countries should nurture their friendship “in the service of a fairer world”. Ecuador President Daniel Noboa “Our region has common enemies, shared challenges, and much to gain when we work together,” Noboa wrote on X, congratulating Lula. Paraguayan President Santiago Pena “I salute the Brazilian people for this great democratic journey,” Pena wrote on X. “Paraguay and Brazil share a common agenda of integration and development. We will continue working together for the wellbeing of our people.” Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi Orsi wrote on X that he had just spoken with his “friend” Lula and congratulated him “on the victory and on the democratic celebration that an electoral process represents”. Argentina’s former President Cristina Kirchner “Congratulations,” Kirchner wrote on X, “first to the Brazilian people”, and also to Lula, for knowing “how to awaken in your compatriots feeling and sense to win this battle”.

items.title: Poultry sold at GH¢80 by farmers reaches consumers at GH¢200 – Dumelo
items.description: Deputy Minister of Food and Agriculture John Dumelo says the government is taking the country’s poultry sector seriously and is committed to addressing challenges affecting local production. Speaking on behalf of the government at a poultry round-table discussion with the Netherlands in Accra on Monday, October 26, Mr Dumelo said data on the sector had highlighted the need for urgent attention and stronger collaboration. “We are taking the poultry sector very seriously,” he said. He also raised concerns about the high cost of locally produced poultry, attributing part of the problem to middlemen who increase prices along the supply chain. Mr Dumelo explained that although farmers could sell poultry at about GH¢80, the price could rise to around GH¢200 by the time it reached consumers. “One thing that is of concern to me is the cost of producing poultry. If you look at the cost of production, the number of middlemen that carry it to the consumer, so yes, even though the farmer sells at affordable prices, maybe GHC80 before it gets to the final consumer, it is around GHC 200, and so let’s look at it,” he noted. READ ALSO: 80% poultry import dependence highlights need to grow local production – Netherlands Ambassador He said the price difference made locally produced chicken less affordable and weakened its competitiveness against imported poultry. The Deputy Minister subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding with the Netherlands Ambassador to Ghana, Hans Akerboom, to strengthen cooperation in the poultry sector. The partnership is expected to support efforts to improve local production through technical expertise, knowledge exchange and investment. The government earlier established the Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative. It is a poultry development programme under the Feed Ghana Programme, launched in November 2025 to boost household poultry farming, improve food security, create jobs and reduce Ghana’s reliance on imported chicken. The government aims to distribute millions of birds and chicks, with support for household producers, small and medium-scale farmers and commercial poultry operators. In July 2026, Feed Ghana Coordinator Bright Demordzi said about 2.5 million birds had been distributed under the initiative. The programme also targets a 50% reduction in poultry imports in the medium term, according to Mr Demordzi. The government has said the initiative is intended to strengthen local production and make Ghana less dependent on imported poultry products.

items.title: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalate
items.description: Parliament authorised Egypt’s military on Monday to provide support to help defend Saudi Arabia, parliamentarians said, and local media reported, a move that could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels on the Gulf kingdom. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had asked parliament last week to approve defending its Gulf Arab ally and the world’s biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requests help against the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic Bab al-Mandeb strait, a gateway to Egypt’s Suez Canal. The House of Representatives “approved authorising President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to take the necessary measures to support the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”, state newspaper Al-Ahram reported. Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian attacks on Gulf countries but has not publicly engaged in direct combat or joined the Makkah mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye that was signed in August. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said this month that Egyptian membership in the pact remains “under serious consideration”. Egypt, the Arab world’s most populous state with one of the region’s largest militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen’s war in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role. Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the 1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War. Saudi Arabia is a major political and financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi. Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran. The Houthis have attacked Riyadh’s international airport and the state oil giant Saudi Aramco, disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises. FM Abdelatty and Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt’s support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said after that visit that Cairo advocates exploring “every opportunity” to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically. The Saudi crown prince visited Sisi in Cairo on Sept 15 to discuss security and navigation in the Red Sea after the fighting in Yemen reignited.

items.title: Netanyahu Goes Into Full Panic Mode
items.description: When the going gets tough, the tough don’t get subtle. Yesterday, with polls casting doubt on his continuing as Israel’s prime minister after Tuesday’s election, Benjamin Netanyahu posted a closing argument on Instagram: an AI-generated image of Tel Aviv destroyed by a nuclear blast, with accompanying text that asked, roughly, Would you prefer to reelect Netanyahu, or be incinerated along with your family? The text—written by the commentator Yuval Bloomberg and reproduced approvingly by Netanyahu—called all of the other campaign issues a “smokescreen,” and accused Netanyahu’s opponents of being so blinded by hatred that they would rather increase their chances of being burned alive than see their country’s political maestro win another election. If you support another candidate, the Instagram post cautioned, “your hand should tremble” as you vote. For years, Israelis both pro- and anti-Netanyahu have advised against counting him out. That advice remains sound. He has a Nixon-like ability to reemerge improbably stronger every time his political career has been declared over. It seemed over on October 7, 2023, when his government presided over an actual mass burning of Israelis. This time, the group of politicians cooperating to drive him from office is diverse and formidable. A former observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet, retired General Gadi Eisenkot, is his chief antagonist. But two allied former prime ministers, the centrist Yair Lapid and center-right Naftali Bennett, are enthusiastic members of the anti-Netanyahu coalition, and another ex-general, Yair Golan, is attacking him from what remains of the Israeli left. These combined efforts have reduced Netanyahu’s chances of remaining in power to one in four, as of this morning. These relatively long odds account, perhaps, for the wild messaging from Netanyahu during the past three days. Netanyahu’s statements have been, as George W. Bush said after Donald Trump’s “American carnage” speech, “some weird shit.” In addition to warning that his opponents will be too beholden to Islamists to stop the flattening of Tel Aviv, Netanyahu’s pronouncements include the assertions that: it is “only a matter of time” before American military assistance for Israel is “over”; that Israel will be beset by international sanctions and compelled to cope without the friends who have in the past guaranteed its survival; and that blockchain-based technologies, such as cryptocurrencies, might provide ways around sanctions. [ Read: Defeating Netanyahu means solving a math problem ] The other candidates have positioned themselves as normal people who can govern Israel competently in difficult times. Bennett replied to the atom-bomb post by calling for the “revival of our international standing,” and declaring his intention to improve the tech sector and force thousands of Israel’s 1.5 million ultra-Orthodox citizens to trade full-time religious study for military service and employment. (Netanyahu and his further-right coalition partners have refused these measures and tried to preserve draft exemptions.) Netanyahu, Yair Lapid wrote , “has gone off the rails. We must send him home.” Netanyahu’s case is that he is an unusual man for unusual times. If the times are not unusual already, he will make them unusual, by shifting Israel’s politics and alliances preemptively—away from America and toward the United Arab Emirates, away from Western financial systems and toward crypto, in a manner reminiscent of sanctions-hobbled regimes like Russia, Iran, and North Korea. There is a logic to this frightening perspective. If you think Israel can be a liberal democracy in a familiar international order, and that competent institutions and international alliances are the way to stave off catastrophe, then vote from the menu of Netanyahu’s opponents. If you think Israel is doomed to being a pariah state, then vote for the guy posting images of his country torched in a nuclear holocaust. Today Avigdor Lieberman, the leader of the secular-nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party, and a member of the anti-Netanyahu club, requested a treason investigation into Netanyahu for intentionally “dragging Israel into war” to improve his electoral chances. This threat of annihilation is not, of course, wholly concocted. But Iran’s open desire to annihilate Israel can be real and still be used as a political pretext to avoid the issues that have led so many Israelis to hate Netanyahu. The same Instagram post that warns of nuclear annihilation helpfully lists these issues: alleged links between Netanyahu and the government of Qatar; reports that Netanyahu received warnings before the October 7 attacks and did nothing; and his support for welfare and draft exemptions for ultra-Orthodox full-time Torah students. About 100,000 such ultra-Orthodox are liable for military service, and most instead study Talmud and are therefore too busy to cram themselves into tanks and fight in Gaza like other Jewish Israelis. Netanyahu’s response to all of these accusations is to crank up the end-of-days volume, to make even the most reasonable criticisms of his politics inaudible. Among secular Israelis, the last of these gripes produces such bitterness that some seem willing to die rather than vote for a politician who would preserve the exemptions. The bitterness stems from the perception that Netanyahu (himself a religious novice) is eager to make unconscionable concessions to the most extreme elements of the ultra-Orthodox political machine in exchange for a few more seats in his coalition. The main ultra-Orthodox parties are Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), both pro-Netanyahu and monomaniacal about preserving exemptions for as many Torah students as possible. [ Graeme Wood: Israel can’t postpone its reckoning forever ] The cynicism of this move is easiest to appreciate not by assaying the venom of secular Israelis but by hearing the dismay of ultra-Orthodox Israelis, also known as Haredim (those who “tremble” before God) unaligned with Shas and UTJ. Ziva Glanz, a candidate for the upstart Haredi Public party, told me with exasperation that the “legacy” parties were immune to change, and that most Haredim were ready to move on, if only the ossified political system would let them. Her party is broadly in the Netanyahu camp, and her party is happy to support Netanyahu’s view of Israel’s security. “Existential problems are existential problems,” she said. But they nonetheless want reform, and see his government and its partners as stopping it. Her party supports reducing the number of draft-exempt Torah students. Glanz, the wife of a rabbi, says she thinks the low civilian casualty rate in Israel’s war with Hezbollah was a miracle granted by God due to Israel’s commitment to religious study. But she says there are 12,000 Haredim who purport to be studying, and whose institutions claim government funds, when in reality they are “hanging out in pizza shops.” They should be put to work. “Our community is a success,” she said, and “with success comes responsibility.” Netanyahu’s response to this modest attempt to disrupt Haredi politics and integrate Haredim into the Israeli national project has been to tell her party to back down. When Netanyahu first won the premiership in 1996, he successfully campaigned on “making a safe peace”—peace guaranteed through Israeli military supremacy, rather than primarily through the negotiation or diplomacy preferred by his rivals. Three decades later, a “safe peace” guaranteed through military might has become so strategically desirable that it unites his rivals—security hawks, one and all—while Netanyahu himself has moved on. He once promised to bring peace. Now he promises that his opponents will bring annihilation. In this account, Israel’s violent devastation is so imminent that corruption, pandering, and venality become mere foibles. But what if ignoring these political vices devastates Israel in slower, less lurid ways? What if limitless draft exemptions, unwillingness to scrutinize past failures, and international isolation are themselves devastating? Tomorrow Israelis will vote, many trembling for the future of their country, no matter which candidate they prefer.

items.title: Counter-Terrorism: Africa must lead in shaping, implementing solutions to challenges – Ribadu
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu has said that Africa must lead in defining, shaping and implementing solutions to the terrorism challenges facing the continent. Ribadu said this reality has become inevitable because, “Terrorist networks move across borders, communicate across platforms and finance their activities through channels that are often transnational. Delivering the keynote address at the High Level African Lessons Learned Forum on Counter-Terrorism Cooperation, Intelligence Sharing and Emerging Technologies’ on Monday, Ribadu said, “No country can address such threats in isolation. We must strengthen mechanisms that allow for timely, trusted and actionable intelligence exchange, while respecting national sovereignty and legal frameworks. The NSA said, “The theme places intelligence sharing at the centre of effective counter-terrorism cooperation. Our partners remain important, and we value their continued support. However, sustainable solutions must be rooted in African ownership, African priorities, African institutions and the lived experiences of our communities. “The theme recognizes the growing role of emerging technologies. Artificial intelligence, digital communications, encrypted platforms, drones, synthetic media and other technological tools that are reshaping the threat landscape. “These technologies present risks when exploited by terrorist groups, but they also offer opportunities for early warning, threat analysis, digital investigation, strategic communications, border security and the protection of vulnerable communities.Our task is to ensure that technology is used responsibly, lawfully and effectively in support of peace and security. “The theme also emphasizes strategic partnerships. Counter-terrorism today requires partnerships among states, regional bodies, international organizations, security agencies, financial intelligence units, communities, civil society, academia, the private sector and technology actors. It also requires trust, consistency and practical cooperation beyond formal declarations. To participants from across the globe, Ribadu said, “Your presence here reflects a shared recognition that the threat of terrorism and violent extremism remains one of the most serious challenges to peace, stability and development across our continent. “This Forum is convened at a time when Africa continues to confront an increasingly complex and adaptive terrorist threat environment. Terrorist groups are exploiting porous borders, local grievances, illicit financial networks, digital platforms, misinformation, online radicalization and emerging technologies. “They are also adapting their methods in ways that challenge traditional security responses. These developments require sustained cooperation, stronger intelligence sharing, coordinated national and regional action, and a deeper commitment to practical lessons learned among African states. “Nigeria’s experience over the past fifteen years has shown that counter-terrorism cannot be sustained through military and kinetic action alone. While security operations remain necessary, they must be complemented by intelligence coordination, law enforcement, financial intelligence, justice, strategic communications, prevention, rehabilitation, reintegration, reconciliation, community resilience, education, youth engagement, research, training and technology-enabled analysis. “This is why Nigeria has continued to advance a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach to counter-terrorism and preventing and countering violent extremism, need for African countries to strengthen real-time intelligence sharing, improve coordination, exchange practical lessons and build trusted professional networks. “It is therefore fitting that we are gathered here under the theme: “Strengthening Africa-Led Counter Terrorism Cooperation through Intelligence Sharing, Technological Innovation and Strategic Partnerships.” The NSA commended the African Union, Regional Economic Communities, the United Nations, the European Union and other partners for advancing practical counter-terrorism cooperation noting, “We are also committed to supporting African-led approaches that place national ownership, regional solidarity and institutional learning at the centre of our collective response. Disclosing that Nigeria is pleased to host the Forum at the National Counter Terrorism Centre because the Centre represents an important part of our national counter-terrorism coordination architecture, Ribadu said, “The NCTC-ONSA has grown as a platform for strategic threat assessment, intelligence fusion, research, training, policy coordination, technology-enabled analysis and non-kinetic programming. It is also increasingly positioned to serve as a continental resource for peer learning and capacity development. “Through this Forum, participants will have the opportunity to engage Nigeria’s experiences, including our efforts in counter-terrorism coordination, preventing and countering violent extremism, strategic communications, countering terrorism financing, rehabilitation and reintegration, and community-based approaches. Initiatives such as Operation SAFE CORRIDOR and the European Union-supported DDRR of Persons “Formerly Associated with Non-State Armed Groups in North-East Nigeria provide lessons on the difficult but necessary connection between security operations, accountability, reintegration, reconciliation and community recovery. “These experiences are not presented as perfect models. Rather, they are offered as practical lessons from which we can all learn. Every country represented here has experience to share. Each of us has confronted challenges, developed institutional responses, recorded successes and encountered setbacks.” The post Counter-Terrorism: Africa must lead in shaping, implementing solutions to challenges – Ribadu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Republic Bank Ghana wins climate finance award at WSBI-ESBG SDG Awards in Bangkok
items.description: Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC has received recognition in the Climate Finance category at the WSBI-ESBG SDG Awards in Bangkok, Thailand, which happened alongside the 2026 IMF Annual Meeting, for its investment in water projects across four locations in Ghana. The award was for the Bank’s contribution to Sustainable Development Goal 6, Clean Water and Sanitation, through mechanized borehole projects at Adidome Senior High School and Taviefe Senior High School in the Volta Region, Pwalugu in the Upper East Region, and Dingoni in the Northern Region. Delivered through the Bank’s Power to Make a Difference (PMAD) initiative, the projects address a fundamental need: reliable access to clean water. The facilities, including solar- and electricity-powered systems, support the daily water needs of students, staff, and underserved communities, strengthening the foundations for better health, education, and livelihoods. The Managing Director, Dr. Benjamin Dzoboku, received the award on behalf of the Bank, marking an important milestone in its commitment to responsible banking and sustainable community development. The recognition highlights the connection between water security and climate resilience. As changing rainfall patterns and water scarcity place pressure on communities, investment in dependable water infrastructure becomes increasingly important. Republic Bank’s interventions show how financial institutions can support practical solutions that meet local needs while advancing broader sustainability goals. Commenting on the recognition, Dr. Dzoboku said: “For us, climate finance must translate into practical benefits for people: a student who can access clean water at school, a family with a dependable water source, and a community better equipped to face environmental challenges. This award affirms our belief that banking should help secure a more sustainable future. We are proud to receive it on behalf of our staff, customers, partners and the communities whose lives these projects touch.” Republic Bank’s Commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals Republic Bank places environmental, social and governance considerations at the heart of its approach to responsible growth. Its sustainability priorities connect environmental stewardship with social inclusion, recognizing that long-term economic progress depends on healthy communities, resilient businesses and the responsible use of natural resources. The Bank’s community investments focus on four Sustainable Development Goals: Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3), Quality Education (SDG 4), Clean Water and Sanitation (SDG 6), and Climate Action (SDG 13). Through these priorities, the Bank seeks to deliver lasting value beyond financial services and make sustainability tangible in the communities it serves. This local commitment is supported by the wider ambition of its parent company, Republic Financial Holdings Limited (RFHL). In September 2026, the Group announced an expanded sustainable finance commitment totaling US$750 million by 2030 across the Caribbean and Ghana, supporting climate action, women-owned and women-led businesses, and agricultural enterprises. For Republic Bank Ghana, the award provides further encouragement to deepen its contribution to sustainable development through purposeful investment and partnerships. The Bank remains committed to supporting initiatives that protect essential resources, strengthen community resilience and create opportunities for future generations.

items.title: Burkina : Consommation des substances psychoactives par les jeunes, ACONTA suscite une dynamique collective et invite à redoubler de vigilance
items.description: La consommation des substances psychoactives par les jeunes, favorisée surtout par l'envahissement des milieux de vie par de nouveaux et nombreux produits avec des designs attrayants, est une situation qui inquiète plus d'un dans la société. Cela est d'autant plus légitime que le rôle des parents (premiers responsables de la protection des enfants) dans la prévention de la consommation de ces substances dangereuses (produits tabagiques, drogues et bien d'autres stupéfiants) est de plus en plus entamé par des contraintes socioprofessionnelles qui leur prennent le temps qu'ils auraient pu consacrer aux enfants. Pourtant, il faut bien veiller à cela, si l'on veut des familles épanouies, une jeunesse saine et, partant, un capital humain à même d'assurer un avenir promoteur au pays. C'est conscient de cet enjeu que l'association Afrique contre le tabac (ACONTA) a, à travers le Projet de renforcement des capacités institutionnelles de ACONTA (PRECI-ACONTA), initié un atelier de sensibilisation et d'échanges réunissant des parties prenantes (structures publiques et privées) de lutte contre le tabac et la drogue au Burkina Faso. L'objectif de ce cadre de réflexion, tenu le 9 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, est de sensibiliser et de mobiliser les principaux acteurs autour de stratégies concertées et efficaces, pour contrer la recrudescence de la consommation du tabac, de la drogue et autres stupéfiants au sein de la population, en particulier chez les jeunes. Cette activité de concertation a d'abord permis de dresser un état des lieux par les communications faites par des spécialistes et structures-ressources. Elle a ensuite permis de dégager des perspectives de lutte, notamment une feuille de route opérationnelle. En effet, et selon le coordonnateur du Programme national de lutte contre le tabac et les autres addictions (PNLTA), O. Éric Doyé, le tabagisme constitue un véritable problème de santé publique dans le monde. Au Burkina, la prévalence tabagique chez les personnes de 18 à 69 ans est de 13,6%, tandis que l'exposition passive à la fumée du tabac à domicile et au lieu de travail est respectivement de 28,3% et 28,6% chez les 18 à 69 ans. Les sujets jeunes de 30 à 44 ans de sexe masculin sont les plus touchés avec une prévalence de 24,3% et les décès imputables au tabac sont estimés à 4 800 par an, dont 1 300 sont des non-fumeurs. Il révèle également que 18% des jeunes consomment un produit électronique contenant de la nicotine et 21,9% se servent de produits de tabac chauffés. Des éléments qui viennent, d'une manière ou d'une autre, corroborer cette enquête menée en septembre 2016 par ACONTA , en collaboration avec l'Alliance pour le contrôle du tabac en Afrique (ACTA), intitulée : « Grands cigarettiers, petites cibles : l'industrie du tabac cible les écoles au Burkina Faso ». Cette étude a révélé que dans la stratégie marketing mise en place par les cigarettiers, les points de vente mobile constituent le mode le plus répandu, avec un total de 86 points de vente recensés autour des seize écoles enquêtées, soit une moyenne d'environ cinq par école. 41 kiosques vendaient des produits du tabac autour de quinze des seize écoles enquêtées. L'étude a, par ailleurs, révélé qu'il y avait 148 points de vente des produits du tabac dans un rayon de 100 mètres autour des seize écoles enquêtées et 81% des écoles ont des points de vente très proches et visibles à partir de leur portail, tandis que 88% des écoles ont dans leurs environs des épiceries vendant des cigarettes dans des paquets de moins de 20 (vente en détail). Une délégation de ACONTA aux côtés de l'Association des étudiants en médecine du Burkina Faso, section USTA, pour une conférence publique sur le phénomène tabagique, le 17 octobre 2026. « Toutes les drogues présentent des risques potentiels pour les jeunes » C'est d'ailleurs sur le phénomène de la drogue que le commissaire principal de police, chef de département de la prévention et du suivi de la législation du Secrétariat permanent du Comité national de lutte contre la drogue (SP-CNLD), N. Lévy Yoda, s'est attardé, en partageant l'expérience de sa structure, dont une des stratégies de prévention est d'impliquer davantage les jeunes, et surtout les parents, dans la lutte contre la consommation de drogues. Pour le spécialiste de la prévention de l'abus des drogues chez les jeunes, les parents sont d'abord les mieux placés dans la prévention, viennent ensuite l'État à travers l'école, les services de santé, l'action sociale, les organisations de la société civile à travers les confessions religieuses, les organisations non gouvernementales, la presse, etc. Au Burkina, fait-il ressortir, le taux de prévalence de la consommation des substances psychoactives est d'environ 6% en milieu scolaire à Ouagadougou. Aussi, suivant qu'elles sont tolérées ou non par les sociétés humaines, les drogues peuvent être classées en deux grands types, renseigne M. Yoda. Ainsi, les « drogues licites » sont celles dont la vente et la consommation ne sont pas interdites par la loi d'un pays, mais réglementées (l'alcool, le tabac, le thé, le cola, etc.) et les « drogues illicites » qui sont celles dont la culture, le trafic, la vente et la consommation sont interdites par la loi d'un pays (cannabis, cocaïne, etc.). « Aucune drogue, quelle qu'elle soit, n'est moins dangereuse qu'une autre pour les adolescents. Toutes les drogues présentent des risques potentiels pour les jeunes », souligne cependant le spécialiste. Lire aussi : Toxicomanie : « La plupart de nos écoles (…) sont des antres de drogue ! », selon Frank Elvis Compaoré du Comité national de lutte contre la drogue. La prévention de la consommation de drogues, comme le tabac, le cannabis… chez les jeunes passe par le renforcement des connaissances de tous sur les dangers liés à la consommation, la maîtrise des facteurs de risques, des facteurs de protection, mais aussi la connaissance des signes d'alerte pour augmenter la prise en charge. Pour cela, le commissaire principal de police, N. Lévy Yoda, a présenté les causes ou facteurs de risques. Il s'agit, et outre l'ignorance, la curiosité et l'imitation (des parents, des stars ou des pairs), de l'absence ou de la non-disponibilité des parents, de la négligence parentale, de l'absence de communication entre parents et enfants (père et fils). Aussi, les violences domestiques dont sont victimes ou témoins les enfants, les attitudes ou propos dévalorisants à leur endroit (l'intolérance des parents envers les enfants (insuffisance au niveau du résultat scolaire, incompréhensions au moment de la puberté, etc.), l'absence de contrôle des fréquentations de l'enfant). L'organisation a entamé une campagne d'apposition d'affiches dans les lieux publics à Ouagadougou. L'expert de la prévention de l'abus des drogues chez les jeunes indique également que l'excès de pression sur les enfants pour des résultats scolaires, le sentiment de ne pas être aimé ou d'être moins aimé par les parents, la séparation des parents, l'absence ou l'insuffisance d'attachement parents-enfant, l'indifférence éducative et l'emprise éducative ainsi que certains troubles mentaux sont des éléments favorisant le basculement. C'est pourquoi, comme facteurs de protection, commissaire Yoda préconise aux parents de mettre en place des mécanismes. Il s'agit d'établir une connexion avec l'enfant (cela va faciliter plus tard la transmission des valeurs sociales) ; lui faire avoir confiance en soi et pouvoir à ses besoins fondamentaux. Le fait de montrer les limites, de savoir les respecter et de les faire respecter est aussi un rôle dévolu aux parents. Il préconise également d'éviter de banaliser les comportements inappropriés devant les enfants (fumer, se saouler,…) et d'établir une bonne communication entre parents, entre parents et enfants, et de ne pas les mettre sous pression tout le temps et de les assurer de son affection et de sa bienveillance (être à l'écoute des enfants), etc. Comme signes d'alerte, on retient que la consommation de drogues entraîne chez les jeunes un changement de comportement qui peut se traduire par l'agressivité soudaine envers les membres de la famille, l'isolement, le manque d'intérêt pour les activités ou distractions habituelles, la disparition d'objets de valeur personnels ou des parents, les absences répétées et non justifiées pour un enfant qui était toujours présent, l'utilisation inhabituelle de parfum ou de déodorant pour dissimuler les odeurs, le changement de comportements (isolement, violence, irritation, passage de la timidité à un courage exceptionnel), la demande incessante d'argent, la baisse de rendement (peut être aussi due au harcèlement, donc nécessite d'aider l'enfant), le changement dans le regard, etc. Tous ces signes doivent interpeller en tant que parent, tuteur, car annonçant très souvent un dysfonctionnement chez l'enfant, qu'il faut identifier et corriger à temps. En cas de problème (découverte d'indices de consommation de drogues), l'expert N. Lévy Yoda recommande de ne pas s'accuser entre parents. « Ne pas se culpabiliser, garder son calme, contacter les services de prise en charge spécialisée », a-t-il orienté avant de conclure par un appel à méditer sur cette pensée d'un homme de Dieu : « De 0 à 7 ans, amuse-toi avec ton enfant. De 7 à 14, enseigne-le. De 14 à 21 ans, devient son ami. À 21 ans, donne-lui sa liberté. » Préserver l'individu, la famille… et le pays ! Selon le médecin-colonel Yiompouén Aimé Somé, cardiologue, la fumée de cigarette comporte plus de 7 000 substances toxiques et plus de 50 substances cancérigènes. Les conséquences sanitaires du tabagisme sont, entre autres, pulmonaires (alvéole chargée du goudron de la fumée du tabac, poumons cancéreux), cardiovasculaires (infarctus du myocarde : arrêt cardiaque), ORL (cancer de la trachée), bucco-dentaires (mauvaise hygiène bucco-dentaire, periodontal, lèvre, langue, cancer de la bouche…), digestives (gastro-duodénaux, brûlures d'estomac, ulcères, cancers), gynéco-obstétricales (impuissance sexuelle, développement fœtal retardé). Outre le poids des décès, le tabac coûte 57 milliards de francs CFA par an à l'économie du Burkina Faso (ce qui équivaut à 0,5 % du PIB en 2020) et les projections situent à 618 milliards de FCFA de perte pour l'économie du Burkina Faso d'ici à 2037. Face aux menaces, l'État burkinabè a adopté de nombreux textes, mis en place des structures de contrôle et renforcé les dispositifs de répression. Ainsi peut-on noter qu'après la ratification de la Convention-cadre de l'OMS pour la lutte antitabac (CCLAT), entrée en vigueur le 29 octobre 2006, et les directives d'application de l'article 8 de la CCLAT (protection contre la fumée de tabac) en 2008, le Burkina a adopté la loi nᵒ 040-2010/AN du 25 novembre 2010 portant lutte contre le tabac au Burkina Faso, suivie du premier décret d'application nᵒ 2011-1052/PRES/PM/MS/MEF abrogé et renforcé par le décret nᵒ 2025-0455 du 16 avril 2025. On peut y ajouter l'arrêté Nᵒ 2021-085 CO/M/DAJC portant interdiction de la consommation de la chicha dans la commune de Ouagadougou. Le pays dispose également, depuis février 2017, d'une unité de sevrage tabagique et, depuis 2025, d'un Programme national de lutte contre le tabac et les autres addictions. Parmi les actions menées dans le cadre de la lutte, on peut retenir les messages sanitaires graphiques (adoption des avertissements sanitaires graphiques depuis 2011, le conditionnement neutre qui est en cours d'implémentation pour renforcer le conditionnement existant, la validation des échantillons des paquets de cigarette avant leur mise sur le marché…). Lire aussi : Vie de famille : « Papa et maman s'insultent jusqu'à 2 h du matin, si je ne prends pas la drogue, je ne peux pas dormir », propos d'un adolescent, cités par Pr Arouna Ouédraogo. Selon les textes en vigueur, au Burkina Faso, il est interdit de fumer dans les lieux publics (qu'ils soient clos ou ouverts) et les transports en commun. Un « lieu public clos » est tout lieu accessible au public couvert par un toit ou entouré par un ou plusieurs murs, quel que soit le type de matériaux utilisés pour le toit, le mûr, qu'il s'agisse d'une structure permanente ou temporaire. Un « lieu public ouvert » est tout lieu non couvert et non entouré accessible au public. Fumer est donc, strictement, interdit dans tous les lieux fermés et couverts affectés à un usage collectif (entreprises, administrations, transports en commun, restaurants, cafés, bars). La loi oblige, de ce fait, les responsables des lieux publics et des transports en commun à afficher de façon apparente l'interdiction de fumer ; à veiller à ce qu'il n'y ait pas de cendriers et d'objets similaires servant de réceptacles des cendres des produits du tabac ; à faire en sorte qu'il n'y ait pas d'objet servant à consommer les tabacs et produits du tabac. La loi fait également obligation à tout responsable de veiller à ce que personne ne fume dans l'établissement, l'entreprise ou le moyen de transport dont il a la charge et de sensibiliser son personnel sur l'interdiction de fumer dans les lieux publics et transports en commun ainsi que de rappeler à l'ordre toute personne fumant dans le lieu ou le transport en commun sous sa responsabilité. Dénoncer, le cas échéant, toute personne refusant de se soumettre à l'interdiction de fumer dans les transports en commun au poste police ou de gendarmerie le plus proche. En cas de violation, le fumeur s'expose à une amende de 15 000 FCFA tandis que les gestionnaires d'établissement (propriétaires des lieux) sont punissables de 50 000 FCFA à 200 000 FCFA. C'est au regard de tout cet enjeu pour les jeunes, les familles, la société et pour le pays que ACONTA a initié, le vendredi 9 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, l'atelier de sensibilisation des parties prenantes sur les stratégies de lutte contre la recrudescence de la consommation du tabac et de la drogue, en particulier chez les jeunes. Il a regroupé des représentants des institutions publiques et des acteurs privés de lutte (programme national de lutte contre le tabac, police municipale, monde éducatif et sanitaire, médias, organisations de la société civile, des partenaires…). Cette journée s'est voulue un espace de dialogue franc et de propositions concrètes, notamment par le partage d'expériences, l'identification des actions prioritaires et la perspective d'une feuille de route consensuelle assortie d'un mécanisme de suivi. Le Coordonnateur de ACONTA, Adama Zango, livrant son discours d'ouverture de l'atelier. Par cet atelier, ACONTA a aussi réitéré son plaidoyer pour l'adoption de la loi révisée de lutte contre le tabac, conforme à la Convention-cadre de l'OMS et intégrant les produits nouveaux et émergents ; l'adoption du décret visant à prévenir l'ingérence de l'industrie du tabac dans les politiques de santé publique, et la finalisation de la mise en œuvre du conditionnement neutre des produits du tabac. « Nous saluons les actions de l'OMS (Organisation mondiale de la santé) et du ministère de la Santé, ainsi que les engagements exprimés par les parlementaires lors de la rencontre de plaidoyer du 22 avril 2026. Nous les remercions pour leur contribution à la protection de la santé publique. La consommation de drogues, comme celle du tabac, appelle une réponse concertée, adaptée aux réalités des jeunes et fondée sur la prévention, l'information, la prise en charge, l'application des textes et l'écoute de leurs préoccupations. Aucun acteur ne peut, à lui seul, relever ce défi. Nos institutions, les familles, les écoles, les médias, les professionnels de santé, les forces de sécurité et la société civile doivent agir en complémentarité », a déclaré le coordonnateur de ACONTA, Adama Zango. À l'issue de l'atelier, et en attendant la mise en œuvre des actions collectives projetées, ACONTA continue de dérouler ses actions de sensibilisation et de veille. C'est dans cette lancée qu'elle a, avec l'accord de la délégation spéciale de Ouagadougou, entamé le samedi 24 octobre 2026, une campagne d'apposition des affiches sur l'interdiction de fumer dans les lieux publics et les transports en commun. Lire aussi : Tabagisme au Burkina : « On va continuer à mener la lutte ensemble. » exhortations du ministre Kargougou à ACONTA O.L. Lefaso.net

items.title: Centre/ Cameroun : Atanga Nji sonne la mobilisation contre l’insécurité
items.description: © DR Le ministre de l'Administration territoriale a réuni le 26 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé les autorités administratives pour évaluer la situation sécuritaire de la région du Centre après la présidentielle du 12 octobre 2025. Face à la montée de l’insécurité, l’État affiche sa fermeté. Paul Atanga Nji a présidé une réunion de sécurité avec le gouverneur de la région du Centre, le préfet du Mfoundi, le maire de la ville de Yaoundé et les responsables régionaux des forces de maintien de l’ordre. Les constats sont alarmants : recrudescence de la criminalité urbaine et interurbaine, féminicides récurrents dans plusieurs départements, agressions dans les taxis et à domicile, vols à main armée, vols aggravés, bandes criminelles organisées et assassinats ciblés. À cela s’ajoutent le trafic de drogue, les accidents mortels quotidiens impliquant des motos-taxis et les agressions de passagers par certains conducteurs. Pour apporter des réponses concrètes, une deuxième réunion sera consacrée au désordre urbain dans le Mfoundi, avec le maire de Yaoundé et les syndicats de motos-taxis. Le ministre a rappelé que la mission régalienne de l’État est de protéger les personnes et leurs biens, et a appelé la population à coopérer pleinement avec les forces de l’ordre pour démasquer les malfaiteurs qui vivent parmi nous. Cet article Centre/ Cameroun : Atanga Nji sonne la mobilisation contre l'insécurité est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Savannah Region prepares to enforce nationwide Styrofoam ban from January 2027
items.description: The Savannah Regional Minister, Salisu Be-Awuribe, has reaffirmed the region’s commitment to enforcing the nationwide ban on Styrofoam products from January 1, 2027, warning that the production, importation, distribution, sale and use of the products will no longer be permitted after the deadline. He said the enforcement forms part of the government’s efforts to protect the environment, improve public health, reduce flooding and preserve the region’s tourism potential. ‎ ‎The Minister made these remarks during a Styrofoam Ban Outreach programme, where he called on residents, traders, food vendors, manufacturers and business operators to prepare for the implementation of the policy. ‎ ‎Mr Be-Awuribe said the Savannah Regional Coordinating Council, the seven Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the Ghana Police Service and customs officers at checkpoints would be expected to ensure strict compliance. ‎ ‎He further warned that vehicles transporting prohibited Styrofoam products would not be allowed into the region after the January 2027 deadline. ‎ ‎The Minister expressed concern over the growing use and improper disposal of Styrofoam takeaway containers in communities across the region, including Damongo, Bole, Sawla, Buipe, Salaga and Daboya. According to him, the products have become a major source of litter, with discarded takeaway containers choking gutters, obstructing drains and contributing to flooding. ‎ ‎He also warned that Styrofoam waste poses a threat to domestic animals and wildlife, particularly elephants at the Mole National Park, which could mistake the discarded materials for food. ‎ ‎He added that burning Styrofoam releases harmful smoke that can affect human health and pollute the environment. ‎ ‎The regional Minister also raised concerns about the potential health risks associated with placing hot foods in certain Styrofoam containers, stressing the need for safer food-packaging alternatives. The specific health risks, however, depend on the materials used and the conditions under which they are heated. ‎ ‎The Minister maintained that the region could not achieve its tourism ambitions while communities and roads remained littered with takeaway containers. ‎ ‎“Savannah Region cannot develop tourism with litter. No tourists will come to see Mole if the road from Fufulso to Damongo or from Bole to Mole is littered with takeaway containers,” he said. Recognising the potential financial challenges the ban could pose to food vendors and traders, the Regional Minister said the EPA’s Savannah Regional Office had been directed to engage stakeholders across markets and communities to educate them on affordable alternatives. ‎ ‎He identified paper packaging, biodegradable containers, reusable bowls and traditional food-wrapping materials as possible substitutes for Styrofoam products. ‎ ‎He, however, encouraged young people in the region to take advantage of the policy by investing in the production and supply of environmentally friendly packaging materials. ‎ ‎He said government programmes, including those operated by the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA) and the Youth Employment Agency (YEA), could provide opportunities for young entrepreneurs interested in developing local alternatives. ‎ ‎Hon. Be-Awuribe further indicated that the government was working to reduce the cost of paper packaging by supporting local factories. ‎ ‎He urged traders and food vendors to cooperate with the authorities during the transition, emphasising that education and partnership would be prioritised over punishment. ‎ ‎As part of preparations for the enforcement deadline, the Minister announced a regional clean-up and public education campaign to run from October through December 2026. The campaign will target chop bars, restaurants, hotels, guest houses, shops, plastic retailers, schools, lorry stations and other businesses and public spaces. ‎ ‎Mr Salisu Be-Awuribe revealed that EPA would engage affected groups in local languages to ensure that residents understand the reasons for the ban, the products affected and the alternatives available. ‎ ‎The Minister cautioned that offenders could face sanctions under the applicable environmental laws, referring to fines of up to GH¢50,000 or imprisonment of up to two years, as outlined in his address. ‎ ‎”The government’s primary objective was to secure voluntary compliance rather than impose penalties on individuals and businesses. ‎ ‎“I do not want any individual, groups, institutions, or businesses to be fined. I want TOTAL compliance through partnership and understanding,” the Minister reiterated ‎ ‎He recalled that President John Dramani Mahama publicly announced the policy on World Environment Day, June 5, 2025, and subsequently declared nationwide enforcement from January 2027 on May 25, 2026. ‎ ‎He described the ban as an important step towards improving environmental cleanliness and protecting communities from the consequences of improper waste disposal. ‎ ‎Mr Be-Awuribe also highlighted the Savannah Region’s importance as Ghana’s largest region by land area, its contribution to food production in northern Ghana and its tourism assets, particularly the Mole National Park. ‎ ‎He called on traditional authorities, local government officials, civil society organisations, the media, traders and the general public to support the initiative. ‎ ‎The Minister concluded by urging residents to take collective responsibility for maintaining a clean environment, declaring that a cleaner region would contribute to better health, stronger tourism and improved economic opportunities. ‎ ‎“Clean Savannah, healthy Savannah, rich Savannah,” he said, calling on residents to work together to keep the region clean. ‎ ‎The outreach programme forms part of efforts to intensify public education ahead of the January 1, 2027 enforcement deadline, as authorities seek to prepare businesses and residents for the transition away from Styrofoam products.

items.title: Nigeria needs 9% annual growth to reduce poverty – Soludo
items.description: Governor Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra says Nigeria needs an annual economic growth of at least nine per cent to significantly reduce poverty and create jobs. He made the assertion at the Nigerian Economic Summit 32 (NES32) with the theme “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity” in Abuja on Monday. He said that Nigeria’s current growth rate of about four per cent remained inadequate to achieve rapid poverty reduction and employment generation. The governor also said that Nigeria would require an annual growth of at least 12 per cent to achieve a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2030 or 2040. He added that the country’s investment rate, estimated at 17 to 20 per cent, must rise significantly to support the required economic expansion. Soludo cautioned against being misled by large nominal spending figures, saying that consolidated public expenditure across all government levels amounted to less than one dollar per person daily. He stressed the need to channel national savings into productive investments, capable of expanding economic output, creating jobs and improving living standards. He called for stronger coordination between the federal government, states and local governments, noting that subnational authorities accounted for a substantial share of public spending. According to him, effective collaboration is essential to maximise the impact of government policies and investments across the country. Soludo cited Anambra’s free education programme, which covers kindergarten through secondary school, as an example of interventions delivering measurable social benefits. He said that the state had reduced its out-of-school children rate from 2.5 per cent to 0.25 per cent. He also cited a recent Oxford and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report which reportedly placed Anambra’s multidimensional poverty rate at 9.6 per cent. Soludo said that reducing food prices required structural reforms to address post-harvest losses, which he put at about 43 per cent of agricultural output. He said that improving storage, transportation and distribution systems would help to move food from farms to urban markets and reduce consumer prices. The governor, therefore, urged governments to strengthen sectoral collaboration and mobilise investments to accelerate economic growth. Soludo also called for policies that encourage exports, develop domestic value chains and promote investment in sectors where Nigeria has competitive advantages. He emphasised that stronger private-sector participation and productive investments were essential to generating sustainable jobs and ensuring that economic growth benefitted more Nigerians. ( NAN ) The post Nigeria needs 9% annual growth to reduce poverty – Soludo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Talks with Makkah pact countries begin in Tehran: Iranian state media
items.description: Officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye are currently meeting in Tehran, according to Iranian state media. The meeting brings together Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to discuss “regional cooperation, the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its consequences”, among other topics, Iran’s state broadcaster said. Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster shared a video of the meeting, saying the quadrilateral meeting on “regional security and stability” had begun. The video showed Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi sitting with Iran’s President Masour Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Earlier in the day, Inter-Services Public Relations had confirmed that Field Marshal Munir was visiting Tehran, but did not share any further details. State-run PressTV also shared pictures of the meeting. Earlier, Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency quoted the deputy secretary of Iran’s top security body, Ali Bagheri Kani, as saying that the visit was part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia. Kani also told state TV that among the visiting dignitaries would be Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, said during a media briefing that the meeting with officials from the three countries would cover “most pressing issues threatening our region”, which included Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in Palestine and Lebanon. He added that the topic of “top priority on the agenda would be consequences of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its ramifications for the entire region”. IRNA further quoted him as saying that this meeting could be a prelude to further steps towards shaping “endogenous security — an issue that we have been insisting on for decades”. “We emphasise that regional security will not be ensured except by relying on the … security considerations of the countries of the region,” he said, adding that events of the last two years, especially the past eight months, had shown that sustainable and reliable security would only be made possible by “building trust and cooperation among the countries in the region”. Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly also confirmed the visit in a post on X. Krimly described the visit as “part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Defence Alliance members for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis, and promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by Qatar and Pakistan”. “The visit underscore the pivotal role of Makkah Defence Alliance members in reinforcing regional security and stability, and working with all countries in the region to achieve that goal,” he added. The visit comes as attacks by Houthis have spiralled over recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated. Monday’s planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. CDF Munir had visited Iran last week as well. During the visit, Iranian leaders had conveyed that the US must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations. According to Iran’s ISNA news agency, Baqaei said during the media briefing that the suggestion for the meeting was made during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran last week. Tehran reviewed the proposal “favourably … and it is scheduled to be held today”, he added. War has engulfed the Middle East since late February when the US and Israel launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, just as Washington and Tehran were in the middle of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme. An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel. Iran claims control over the strait and regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross without its authorisation, while the United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal which laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement. The war has since spread across the region to include fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.

items.title: Ex-Premier League star needs 50 stitches after German Shepherd attack
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant has revealed that he needed more than 50 stitches after a German Shepherd mauled his leg in north London, with his own dog intervening to help fight off the attacker. According to the BBC, the 43-year-old former Liverpool and Stoke City winger was walking his two dogs last week when the German Shepherd latched on to his right leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his dog, King. Pennant said King eventually intervened and fought off the attacking dog, preventing what he described as a potentially horrific situation. “I tried to protect King but the dog got my leg, I was on the floor with the dog still attached with no sign of letting go, until King intervened as he didn’t know what was going on,” Pennant said. He told The Sun that he suffered four bite wounds and required more than 50 stitches after receiving hospital treatment. Although King sustained a small bite, Pennant said his dog was otherwise unharmed. He recalled feeling more concerned about King when he saw blood covering the animal, before realising it was not his. Pennant later shared a photograph on Instagram showing himself with his injured leg bandaged and King beside him on a sofa, describing the dog as his “hero” and thanking his partner, Mimmi Montgomery, for caring for them both. The former footballer also said he chose not to report the attack to the police. He did not provide further details about the German Shepherd or its owner. Pennant made 231 Premier League appearances during a 19-year playing career before retiring in 2018. He represented clubs including Liverpool and Stoke City and later became a football pundit for TalkSPORT. He joined Arsenal from Notts County in 1999 for £2.5 million at the age of 15, becoming the most expensive trainee in English football at the time. items.title: Cameroun : le gouvernement ouvre une enquête sur les oeufs et poulets
items.description: © (DR) Après une étude nationale dénonçant la présence présumée de métaux lourds, de résidus d’antibiotiques et de toxines dans les œufs et le poulet de grande consommation, le ministre de la Santé publique annonce des investigations. En attendant les résultats, il appelle à la vigilance sans céder à la panique. Le gouvernement monte au créneau. Dans un communiqué daté du 23 octobre 2026, le ministre de la Santé publique, Dr Manaouda Malachie, informe l’opinion publique que des investigations sont en cours. Elles font suite à une dénonciation issue d’une étude nationale sur la qualité sanitaire des œufs et du poulet destinés à la grande consommation. L’objectif est politique autant que sanitaire : évaluer les risques éventuels, mesurer l’ampleur de la situation et, le cas échéant, prendre des mesures appropriées en collaboration avec les administrations compétentes. Le ministre entend ainsi rassurer, tout en montrant que l’État prend l’alerte au sérieux. En attendant les résultats, le Dr Manaouda Malachie invite les consommateurs à privilégier les œufs et le poulet provenant de sources fiables, clairement identifiées par les services de l’État et respectant les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène, de conservation et de manipulation. Il réitère enfin son appel à la vigilance et à la dénonciation de toute situation suspecte, et réaffirme l’engagement du gouvernement à renforcer la sécurité sanitaire des aliments sur toute l’étendue du territoire national. Cet article Cameroun : le gouvernement ouvre une enquête sur les oeufs et poulets est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Northern leaders must share blame for region’s backwardness – Gov Uba Sani
items.description: Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has said political office holders in Northern Nigeria since 1999 must accept responsibility for the region’s developmental challenges, including its high number of out-of-school children. Sani made the remarks while defending President Bola Tinubu’s record in office, arguing that Northern leaders should not blame the current administration alone for problems that have persisted for decades. “I’m a northerner, and I’m telling you that anybody who held position, whether a governor, minister, senator, vice president, you should be ready to take blame,” he said. The governor cited figures on out-of-school children, stating that Nigeria had about 18 million children out of school as of 2023, with approximately 70 per cent living in Northern Nigeria. He questioned whether Tinubu, who assumed office in May 2023, should be held solely responsible for a crisis that predates his administration. Sani also disclosed that Kaduna State had about 550,000 out-of-school children when he assumed office in 2023, claiming that his administration had returned 300,000 of them to classrooms. He urged political leaders to move away from regional sentiments in their campaigns, insisting that voters should assess candidates based on their records in public office rather than their geographical origins. “The people of Northern Nigeria are very smart. You cannot come to them and tell them, ‘Vote for me because I’m a northerner.’ They will never vote for you. They can only vote for you based on your track record,” he said. The governor also highlighted federal road projects in the North-East and North-West as evidence of infrastructure development under Tinubu. According to him, more than 348 kilometres of roads had been completed in the North-East, while about 3,100 kilometres were under construction. He added that approximately 1,800 kilometres of the ongoing projects were nearing 90 per cent completion. In the North-West, Sani said more than 342 kilometres of roads had been completed, while another 1,042 kilometres were nearing 90 per cent completion. On education financing, the governor said more than 414,000 students from the North-West had benefited from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), with about N84 billion allocated to the region. He described the student loan scheme as an intervention for young people from low-income households who might otherwise struggle to finance their education. Sani further stressed the importance of technical and vocational education and training (TVET), saying skills development was essential to addressing unemployment and expanding opportunities for young people in Northern Nigeria. He maintained that education remained critical to the region’s development and urged political leaders to focus on policies and programmes that improve the lives of residents. The post Northern leaders must share blame for region’s backwardness – Gov Uba Sani appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: From Survival to Scale: How fintech apps are rewiring Ghana’s MSME economy
items.description: With a $4.8 billion financing gap and over 90% of small businesses locked out of formal credit, a new generation of Ghanaian fintech platforms is building the digital rails that keep the economy’s backbone moving, and iSmart and Korba are showing how it’s done. Ghana’s micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are not just a segment of the economy; they are the economy. They constitute over 90% of all registered businesses, contribute roughly 70% of Gross Domestic Product, and provide around 80% of total employment, with an estimated 1.7 million businesses employing about 8.5 million people. Yet for decades, this formidable engine has been running on a persistent and punishing constraint: access to finance. The Bank of Ghana (BoG) identifies an annual SME financing gap of approximately $4.8 billion, a chasm that has widened even as the country’s digital payment infrastructure has exploded. The paradox is striking. In June 2026 alone, mobile money platforms processed 954 million transactions valued at approximately GH¢493 billion, up more than 50% from the GH¢323 billion recorded a year earlier. Some 82% of all financial transactions in Ghana now happen digitally, supported by over 26 million active mobile money accounts. Ghana has built “extraordinary payment rails,” as BoG Second Deputy Governor Matilda Asante-Asiedu put it, but has “not yet built equally extraordinary credit rails”. Over 90% of SMEs still have zero access to formal credit. It is within this gap between the ubiquity of digital payments and the scarcity of digital credit that a quiet revolution is taking place. Ghanaian fintech companies are no longer simply moving money; they are building the operational, transactional, and trust infrastructure that allows MSMEs to professionalise, scale, and, eventually, become bankable. Two platforms in particular, iSmart and Korba, illustrate how solving unglamorous, ground-level problems is creating the conditions for broader economic participation. iSmart: Building the Full-Stack Digital Utility for the Small Enterprise Founded in Accra in 2015, iSmart International Ghana has evolved from a value-added services (VAS) provider into an ISO- and PCI-DSS-certified digital infrastructure company serving over 10,000 clients, from major banks and telecoms to small enterprises. Its proposition is not a single app but a suite of tools that meet MSMEs where they are: often on basic feature phones, often in rural areas, often without the luxury of time to learn complex software. At the heart of its MSME offering is iSmart Pay, a payment platform developed just over a year ago to help businesses receive and manage payments through three channels: mobile money, direct bank transfers, and the iSmart Pay wallet. For a market trader or a small retail shop, this eliminates the friction of maintaining separate merchant accounts for each network. For a growing enterprise, iSmart’s payment APIs and gateways provide the flexibility to integrate collections directly into their own operations. But iSmart’s deeper contribution lies in the unglamorous plumbing that keeps small businesses connected. Its USSD connectivity allows any MSME or its customers to check balances, pay bills, or access services by dialling a short code, no internet required. This “no internet, no problem” approach brings essential digital functions to millions who remain outside the smartphone economy. Meanwhile, its Customer Engagement Solutions (CESI) platform, which includes tools like Digitalk, CPaaS, and Grow, empowers telecoms, enterprises, and SMEs to manage and engage over 4.5 million subscribers across Africa, turning one-way transactions into ongoing commercial relationships. The strategic logic is clear. As research on fintech adoption among Ghanaian MSMEs has found, the perceived ease of use is the strongest driver of adoption, and the real competitive advantage emerges only when digital tools are deeply integrated into core business processes, yielding gains in cost efficiency, operational agility, and service differentiation. iSmart’s stack is designed for exactly that integration: a small business can start with bulk SMS for marketing, graduate to USSD for customer self-service, and layer on iSmart Pay for collections, all within a single, certified ecosystem. Korba: Restoring Trust and Turning Agents into Micro-Hubs If iSmart builds the broad infrastructure, Korba (operated by Halges) attacks two of the most visceral pain points facing Ghanaian businesses that accept digital payments: the fear of reversals and the struggle of mobile money agents to earn a sustainable living. Payment reversals have been a silent killer for Ghanaian merchants. A customer pays, the business releases the product, and then the customer reverses the transaction back into their wallet. Korba estimates that businesses across Ghana have lost “well over 10 million cedis” to this practice, with restaurants, delivery companies, retail shops, and online vendors bearing the brunt. KorbaPay was built to eliminate this vulnerability: when a customer pays through the platform, the funds stay with the business, and the customer cannot initiate a reversal from their end. For a small online vendor or a delivery startup operating on thin margins, this is not a feature; it is the difference between staying in business and closing shop. It restores the confidence necessary for digital commerce to function. At the same time, Korba has built a parallel solution for the army of mobile money agents and small business owners who form the last-mile distribution network of Ghana’s financial system. The Korba Agent app turns an ordinary smartphone into a point-of-sale (POS) terminal, allowing agents to offer a far wider range of services beyond basic cash-in and cash-out: airtime and data sales across all networks, utility bill payments for DStv, GOTV, StarTimes, ECG, and Ghana Water, insurance sales, and event ticketing, each earning instant commissions. For an agent whose income was previously limited to a narrow spread on mobile money transactions, this diversification can “significantly boost their income,” as the app’s own description puts it. Korba has also addressed the cost barrier. Its payment solution for businesses is priced at as low as 1.5% per transaction, with a cap for example, a fixed GHS 20 fee on transactions above GHS 3,000. This predictable, capped pricing structure is particularly important for higher-value MSME transactions, where percentage-based fees can erode already thin margins. The Wider Ecosystem and the Road Ahead iSmart and Korba are not isolated success stories. They are part of a maturing ecosystem that includes platforms like Oze, which combines digital bookkeeping with lending and has served over 10,000 SMEs and is remaking cross-border remittances; Fido, which has issued over $500 million in digital loans; and Hubtel, whose merchant payment and USSD products power tens of thousands of businesses. The Bank of Ghana is actively pushing this frontier, advancing open banking and open finance frameworks with the explicit goal of turning mobile money transaction records into usable credit histories. As Second Deputy Governor Asante-Asiedu argued, “This is not just background information. It is a credit record. We have simply not built the habit of reading it as such”. The challenges remain formidable: regulatory fragmentation, cybersecurity risks, data governance gaps, and inadequate digital infrastructure in some regions. But the direction of travel is unmistakable. The fintech applications that are transforming MSMEs in Ghana are not doing so by replicating traditional banking. They are doing it by embedding financial services into the daily workflows of small businesses through a USSD menu that works on any phone, a payment gateway that accepts whatever the customer has, an agent app that turns a kiosk into a multi-service hub, and a fraud-prevention layer that makes digital transactions safe enough to rely on. For Ghana’s 1.7 million MSMEs, the promise of fintech is not abstract. It is the ability to receive a payment without fear of reversal, to manage customer relationships without a technical team, and to build, transaction by transaction, the digital footprint that one day becomes a credit record. iSmart and Korba are proving that the most impactful innovation often looks less like a shiny new app and more like the invisible rails that allow the backbone of the economy to finally stand upright. – Kweku Hammond – Snr Sales & Marketing Consultant/ Faculty – Nova Business School Africa

items.title: Burkina: contrôle du respect des procédures d’importation et d’exportation
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 25 octobre 2026) Les équipes de la Brigade Mobile de Contrôle Économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) intensifient leurs opérations de contrôle du respect des procédures d’importation et d’exportation. Elles sillonnent les entrepôts afin de vérifier la traçabilité des marchandises importées et exportées. Les contrôles menées par les équipes poursuivent un objectif clair, protéger la santé des consommateurs, tout en préservant le pouvoir d’achat et en luttant contre la fraude et la spéculation La BMCRF rappelle que le respect des procédures d’importation et d’exportation est une obligation. Tout manquement constaté fera l’objet de sanctions. Les commerçants et importateurs sont donc invités à se conformer strictement aux dispositions réglementaires En cas de doute ou de suspicion, 80 00 11 84 | 80 00 11 85 | 80 00 11 86 La BMCRF réaffirme son rôle de bouclier contre les dérives économiques et son engagement à maintenir un marché sain, transparent et équitable.
