items.title: La France veut étendre sa présence nucléaire en Europe avec des avions de combat déployés dans dix pays
items.description: La France cherche a etendre la presence de ses forces nucleaires en Europe dans le cadre d'une initiative visant la Russie, rapporte le Wall Street Journal le 25 octobre. Baptise « dissuasion avancee » par Emmanuel Macron, ce projet prevoit le deploiement de chasseurs Rafale capables d'emporter des missiles nucleaires dans plusieurs pays europeens. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans la doctrine presentee par Macron en mars 2026, sur fond d'incertitudes concernant les garanties de securite americaines . Elle prevoit egalement la creation de nouvelles infrastructures militaires, de systemes d'alerte precoce, de communications securisees et de mecanismes de partage de renseignements entre Paris et ses partenaires. Dix etats participent aux discussions a des degres divers : le Royaume-Uni, l'Allemagne, la Belgique, les Pays-Bas, la Pologne, la Grece, la Finlande, la Norvege, la Suede et le Danemark. La France a constitue un groupe de coordination distinct pour chaque pays et privilegie les negociations bilaterales. L'Italie a refuse de rejoindre l'initiative, tandis que les trois pays baltes n'y participent pas. Le projet vise, selon ses promoteurs, a creer une « incertitude strategique » pour Moscou. Lors d'une conference a Varsovie, Xavier Chatel, conseiller de Macron pour les affaires strategiques, a explique que cette approche obligerait la Russie a prendre en compte un facteur supplementaire dans ses calculs militaires. Elle offrirait egalement a Paris davantage de possibilites de disperser ses forces nucleaires en cas d'escalade. Un dispositif nucleaire controle par Paris Cette extension envisagee du dispositif francais ne s'accompagne toutefois d'aucun partage du pouvoir de decision. La France conservera seule le controle de son arsenal nucleaire et de son eventuel emploi. Macron a affirme que les interets vitaux francais possedaient une dimension europeenne, sans offrir pour autant de garantie explicite de protection a ses partenaires. Le president francais a egalement annonce une augmentation du nombre d'ogives nucleaires, tout en decidant de ne plus communiquer publiquement la taille de l'arsenal national. Les conditions de participation restent par ailleurs a preciser. Le president finlandais Alexander Stubb a exclu tout stationnement d'armes nucleaires en Finlande. Le chef de la diplomatie norvegienne, Espen Barth Eide, a souligne que cette initiative viendrait completer les garanties nucleaires americaines, sans les remplacer. Moscou denonce les risques lies au renforcement nucleaire europeen Les projets francais avaient deja suscite des avertissements de la Russie. Le vice-ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, Alexandre Grouchko, avait prevenu que Moscou prendrait en compte tout eventuel deploiement nucleaire francais sur le territoire d'etats europeens dans sa planification militaire. Le diplomate avait egalement averti que les sites susceptibles d'accueillir de telles armes pourraient devenir des cibles prioritaires pour les forces russes en cas de conflit majeur. L'ambassadeur russe en Allemagne, Sergueï Netchaïev, avait de son cote qualifie le renforcement du « parapluie nucleaire » europeen de menace strategique directe. Il a souligne la necessite de prendre ces projets en compte dans la planification politico-militaire russe. Ces avertissements interviennent alors que Moscou denonce depuis plusieurs annees le renforcement des capacites militaires de l'OTAN a proximite de ses frontieres. La Russie considere cette evolution comme un risque pour sa securite, tandis que l'Alliance tente de presenter ses initiatives comme des mesures de dissuasion.

items.title: Lucky Group, Qatar Energy consortium quits Port Qasim LNG terminal plan over 'policy changes'
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Energas, a consortium of the Lucky Group and Qatar Energy, has given up a multi-million-dollar plan to establish a liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal at Port Qasim, citing fundamental changes to Pakistan’s energy policy, requirements and longstanding unresolved policy and fiscal matters, it emerged on Friday. On the other hand, the Port Qasim Authority (PQA) has warned Energas of terminating its final letter of intent (LOI) unless an “unconditional acceptance” is received on or before Nov 30, 2026, along with an updated status of the project. This would also result in forfeiture of the $2 million initial concession fee, PQA said. Subsequently, Energas has approached the prime minister for the refund of $2m, absolving it of any contractual lapse and instead blaming the government and factors beyond its control for not moving ahead. Informed sources told Dawn that Qatar Energy had booked an LNG terminal and committed to supply additional LNG quantities at around 10.2pc of Brent — almost the same rate it contracted to Pakistan State Oil under a second-term contract — to ensure full utilisation of terminal capacity on its own. Qatar has been seeking pipeline capacity allocation for LNG transportation through the terminal it planned with local partners near Karachi, a level playing field for LNG marketing and a terminal, and exemption from third-party access (TPA) that requires certain terminal capacity for use by government entities. Ahead of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s August 2022 visit to Qatar , Pakistan approved changes to the LNG policy to remove restrictions on upcoming private sector LNG terminals to provide their part capacity to the government. These were officially conveyed to the Qatari counterpart by then-petroleum minister Musadik Malik for re-engaging on LNG sector cooperation, including speedy completion of the LNG terminal and another long-term contract for more gas supplies on top of two existing long-term contracts, in addition to LPG supplies. While the energy situation kept changing, the project could not move forward over the subsequent three years as Pakistan sought diversion of its existing contracted LNG cargoes even before this year’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Feb 28 US-Israel attacks on Iran and suspension of Qatar’s LNG production. Quoting past correspondence, Energas’s chairman Muhammad Ali Tabba complained to PM Shehbaz that PQA was “demanding” Energas’s unconditional acceptance of the final LOI by Nov 30, 2026, failing which PQA will cancel the final LOI and forfeit the $2m initial concession fee paid by Energas. He said the Lucky Group Consortium had taken up a self-funded project in good faith and in response to Pakistan’s energy requirements prevailing at the relevant time, which had since materially changed. “Energas’s inability to proceed with the project is attributable to two critical factors: firstly, a fundamental change in national energy policy and requirements, resulting in a clear frustration of purpose; and secondly, the persistent and longstanding unresolved policy and fiscal matters with the government, PQA and other government bodies/authorities, which have continuously impeded the viability”, he noted. The Energas chairman contended that those issues remain unresolved to date, which could have led to a final investment decision (FID) by Qatar Energy and Pakistani partners. “The government had committed to resolving these matters following discussions with the State of Qatar. However, despite the passage of time, the aforesaid matters remain unresolved, thereby adversely affecting investor interest,” Tabba said. He added that the national energy requirements and the policy environment had materially evolved since the project was originally conceived and Energas had already approached PQA for the return/refund of the partial concession fee. Energas said Pakistan’s official Integrated Energy Study (IES) — Final Report of March 28, 2025 confirmed that no new LNG terminals were required over the next five years. According to Energas, this “unequivocal admission” on the part of the government materially alters the circumstances and context in which the Energas project was conceived and directly affects the necessity and economic rationale for the project, resulting in a clear frustration of purpose from an investor’s perspective. It recalled that at the time of issuance of the provisional LOI in May 2020, the LNG Policy 2011 provided LNG terminal operators with a five-year tax holiday commencing from the Commercial Operations Date, but the exemption was withdrawn in June 2021 for new terminals while existing terminal beneficiaries continued to avail the exemption. This was attributed to conditions imposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF); thus, the proposed LNG terminal became “redundant and infructuous”, Energas said. In its letter to Energas, PQA said the $2m deposited by Energas was not an ordinary refundable advance but an initial/partial concession fee under Clause 2.6(i) of the Project Guidelines 2019 that provides that this amount may be forfeited if the developer fails to fulfil the required conditions within the prescribed time, unless the parties agree otherwise. Furthermore, paragraph 27 of the final LOI required LOI termination and forfeiture of $2m in the absence of unconditional acceptance within the deadline. Highlighting Energas’s reasons regarding pipeline capacity allocation, execution of Gas Transportation Agreements (GTAs) with gas companies, allocation of tie-in area, exemption under TPA Rules and the income-tax exemption issue, PQA asserted that Energas was responsible for these developers’ obligations. “Project Guidelines require the developer to undertake the necessary surveys, investigations, environmental studies, hydraulic studies, detailed design and other project-related studies, and to obtain the requisite governmental and regulatory approvals,” PQA pointed out. It added that it was also the developers’ responsibility to have financing, design, construction, relevant access, regulatory compliance and other project requirements.

items.title: Fatatu Forest, a hidden natural retreat in northern Iran
items.description: TEHRAN - Tucked away in the rural landscape of northern Iran, Fatatu Forest is a natural attraction in Khomam county, Gilan province, offering visitors a peaceful escape among lush vegetation, wetlands, rice fields and the landscapes of the southern Caspian coast. Recognized for its ecological importance and its surviving Hyrcanian forest vegetation, the woodland holds considerable potential for nature-based tourism, although limited visitor facilities remain a challenge.

items.title: Nioro du Rip : le nouveau khalife de Maba Diakhou Ba fait de l’enseignement coranique sa priorité
items.description: Le nouveau khalife de la famille de l’Almamy Tafsir Maba Diakhou Bâ, El Hadji Omar Bâ, veut faire du renforcement de l’enseignement coranique et de la transmission du savoir islamique une priorité de son mandat, afin de préserver l’héritage religieux de cette famille. Selon un communiqué de sa cellule de communication, cette orientation a été annoncée ce week-end à Nioro du Rip, lors d’une rencontre avec ses proches collaborateurs et des représentants des différentes cellules de la communauté. La rencontre a aussi été marquée par des actes d’allégeance à la nouvelle autorité religieuse. Le khalife entend promouvoir l’apprentissage du Coran et l’éducation islamique à Nioro du Rip, ainsi que dans les autres localités liées à l’héritage de Tafsir Maba Diakhou Bâ. Ancien enseignant coranique et éducateur religieux, il a invité les membres de sa communauté à s’investir davantage dans la quête du savoir religieux et dans la pratique des valeurs de l’islam. Parlant en son nom, l’imam Aliou Bâ a insisté sur la nécessité de sauvegarder l’héritage spirituel de Tafsir Maba Diakhou Bâ et de son frère Mamour Ndary Bâ. « Le foyer allumé par Tafsir Maba Diakhou Bâ pour le triomphe de l’islam doit toujours être illuminé et l’école coranique doit en rester le pilier », a-t-il déclaré. La question du financement de l’enseignement religieux a également été abordée. Le directeur de l’Institut islamique Tafsir Maba Diakhou Bâ de Nioro du Rip, Malick Elimane Tafsir Mamour Bâ, a déploré le manque de subventions, qu’il considère comme un frein au bon fonctionnement de cet établissement franco-coranique. Sur le plan organisationnel, le khalife a confié à l’ancien gouverneur El Hadji Malick Bâ la coordination de l’ensemble des activités de la communauté. Les structures existantes et leurs responsables devraient, pour l’essentiel, être maintenues dans un souci de continuité. Des prières ont enfin été formulées pour le repos de l’âme de l’ancien khalife, El Hadji Mamour Ndiogou Bâ, décédé le 1er octobre dernier, ainsi que pour la paix au Sénégal et dans le monde. L’imam Aliou Bâ a, de son côté, appelé au raffermissement des relations avec les différentes communautés religieuses.

items.title: TOR records GH¢1.24bn profit in 2025 after a decade of losses
items.description: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) recorded a profit before tax of GH¢1.24 billion in 2025, marking its first return to profitability in a decade, Managing Director Edmond Kombat has disclosed. He attributed the financial improvement to prudent management, improved commercial operations and measures introduced to strengthen the refinery’s financial position following years of losses and mounting liabilities. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said the refinery had made significant progress in addressing its financial challenges under the administration of President John Dramani Mahama. He said the company’s trade and other payables declined from GH¢7.1 billion to GH¢5 billion within a year, while its receivables days dropped from 1,099 to 652. “What matters more is that trade and other payables fell from GH¢7.1 billion to GH¢5 billion in a single year, and receivable days fell from 1,099 to 652,” he stated. The Managing Director said the improved financial performance reflected management’s efforts to rebuild the company’s commercial operations, strengthen accountability and restore confidence among business partners. According to him, commercial operations generated more than 36 per cent revenue growth in 2025 compared with 2024, with revenue increasing by almost 60 per cent as of September 2026. He said management had also recovered outstanding receivables, improved financial controls and continued upgrading the refinery’s Quality Control Laboratory. The results represent a significant shift from the financial position inherited in May 2025, when the refinery had accumulated losses of approximately GH¢10 billion and debt estimated at US$517 million. Mr Kombat said management was also pursuing a financial restructuring programme, including independent assessments of liabilities and discussions with the Ghana Revenue Authority, SSNIT and other creditors to establish sustainable repayment arrangements. He added that the Ministry of Finance was working with TOR to consider writing off US$120 million in legacy debt owed to the government or converting the amount into equity. Mr Kombat said management remained focused on sustaining the financial gains and improving performance in 2026. “The team is focused to deliver even better results for 2026,” he said.

items.title: We are spending where it matters most, five statutory funds paid in full – Ato Forson
items.description: Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson says the government is directing spending towards essential services Ghanaians rely on, following the timely and full payment of third-quarter allocations to five statutory funds. In a social media post, the Minister linked the payments to the everyday needs of citizens, including education, healthcare, roads and community development. “We are spending where it matters most, on the services Ghanaians depend on every day,” he stated. The five funds are the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund), the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF), the Ghana Medical Trust Fund and the Road Maintenance Trust Fund. An accompanying Ministry of Finance graphic indicated that all five had received their third-quarter payments for 2026 in full. “These five funds have received their third-quarter payments on time and in full, supporting schools, healthcare, roads and development in our communities,” Dr Forson said. The Minister emphasised the human significance of meeting these obligations, pointing to the people who depend on the services the funds support. “Behind every payment are people whose needs cannot wait,” he added.

items.title: LFR 2026 : la Banque centrale alerte sur les risques inflationnistes et appelle à une discipline budgétaire
items.description: Devant les députés de l’Assemblée nationale, le samedi 24 octobre 2026, Mohamed Lamine Conté, premier vice-gouverneur de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG), a souligné les enjeux économiques du projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026. Il a notamment insisté sur la maîtrise de l’inflation, la préservation des réserves de change et la nécessité de concilier financement public et investissement privé. Dans un contexte international marqué par la hausse des prix de l’énergie et les tensions sur les marchés, l’économie guinéenne affiche des perspectives de croissance estimées à 8,6 % en 2026, contre 7,1 % en 2025. Cette dynamique est notamment portée par le secteur minier et la montée en puissance du projet Simandou, dont les recettes attendues pour l’Etat sont estimées à environ 350 millions de dollars cette année. Toutefois, le premier vice-gouverneur a mis en garde contre les risques liés à cette manne financière, notamment les pressions inflationnistes et les déséquilibres susceptibles d’affecter les secteurs non miniers. L’inflation, après avoir atteint 6,4 % en juillet, s’est établie à 5,9 % en septembre 2026, principalement sous l’effet de la hausse des prix des produits alimentaires. Sur le plan monétaire, la BCRG entend maintenir une approche prudente, tout en favorisant le financement de l’économie. Mohamed Lamine Conté a également souligné l’importance du renforcement des réserves de change, de la stabilité du franc guinéen et de la modernisation du système financier. Concernant la LFR 2026, il a attiré l’attention des députés sur trois priorités : préserver la stabilité des prix, éviter que le recours accru à l’emprunt public ne réduise les financements destinés au secteur privé et améliorer la coordination entre la politique budgétaire, la gestion de la trésorerie de l’État et la politique monétaire. Pour la BCRG, la réussite de cette loi rectificative dépendra de la capacité des autorités à transformer les ressources minières en investissements productifs, en emplois et en développement durable, tout en préservant les équilibres macroéconomiques du pays.

items.title: CICMG calls for flexible lending conditions to expand credit access
items.description: The Chartered Institute of Credit Management, Ghana (CICMG), is calling for more flexible lending conditions, increased credit capital and stronger financial literacy programmes to improve access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and informal-sector operators. President of the Institute, Evelyn Osei Tutu, says stringent collateral requirements, high interest rates and inadequate borrower education are limiting access to credit, particularly for businesses and individuals in rural communities. Speaking at the 2026 Ghana Credit Excellence Awards in Accra, she urged banks, regulators and policymakers to balance responsible lending with measures that allow more viable businesses to access financing. “It’s making facilities a bit slow when banks are issuing to the SMEs because some of them don’t really have the requirements,” she said. Mrs Osei Tutu acknowledged the importance of credit assessment in preventing defaults but argued that overly rigid lending conditions could discourage potential borrowers. “If we are able to get more capital injected and if the regulators also make things a little flexible. I think we should be able to do more, especially with the rural areas and other markets we manage with the informal sector too,” she added. Mrs Osei Tutu also identified financial literacy as essential to improving repayment rates, saying borrowers must understand their obligations before accessing credit. “You realise that we are very much in a hurry to give out the credits to people, but we don’t tell them the consequences of what you tend to benefit and the things that you have to do right,” she said. She called for stronger education programmes for borrowers and credit officers, alongside improved loan monitoring and recovery systems. “Loans are easy to give but they are difficult in recovery,” she said, warning that inadequate guidance could result in borrowers mismanaging facilities and lenders losing their investments. Meanwhile, General Manager of Emmanuel Cooperative Credit Union, William Atta-Pearce, says credit unions can help address financing gaps among rural borrowers who struggle to meet conventional bank collateral requirements. “Many individuals, particularly those in rural areas, are denied of credit because of issue of collateral, but we as Credit Union, that is where we come in, so that we make credit accessible for such individuals,” he said. He explained that credit unions can extend financing to borrowers who lack property to use as security while relying on their structures to support loan recovery. Mr Atta-Pearce, whose institution was recognised as Cooperative Credit Union Brand of the Year at the awards, called for efforts to expand access to credit regardless of borrowers’ locations. “I think that it’s high time we look at how we can make credit accessible, irrespective of wherever you are, so that people can easily get access to money and that will also help us to grow the economy,” he said. Both credit management professionals stressed the need to improve access to financing while maintaining responsible lending practices, effective borrower education and mechanisms to ensure loan repayment.

items.title: Guinée : 8,6 % de croissance en 2026, plusieurs milliards pour accélérer Simandou 2040 (Ismaël Nabé)
items.description: el NabéLors de la présentation du projet de Loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026, samedi 24 octobre au Palais du Peuple, le ministre de la Coopération, du Plan et du Développement, Ismaël Nabé, a mis en avant les perspectives économiques de la Guinée, les engagements financiers de ses partenaires et les priorités du programme Simandou 2040. La Guinée table sur une croissance économique de 8,6 % en 2026, malgré un taux d’inflation projeté à 5,2 %, dans un contexte international marqué par les tensions géopolitiques. Devant les députés et les responsables institutionnels, Ismaël Nabé a insisté sur la nécessité de traduire ces performances attendues en emplois, en revenus, en infrastructures et en services sociaux de qualité. Le ministre a également souligné les avancées enregistrées dans la production des données statistiques, avec les résultats du quatrième Recensement général de la population et de l’habitation, la sixième Enquête démographique et de santé et le lancement de la deuxième Enquête harmonisée sur les conditions de vie des ménages. Le premier Recensement général des entreprises doit, par ailleurs, permettre de mieux orienter les investissements et de renforcer l’accompagnement des petites et moyennes entreprises. Sur le plan financier, les ressources attendues de la coopération internationale pour la période 2025-2026 sont estimées à 284,8 millions de dollars. Parmi les engagements annoncés figurent 170 millions de dollars de la Banque arabe pour le développement économique en Afrique pour le projet de l’Université de Kankan, 50 millions de dollars du Fonds saoudien pour le développement sur la période 2026-2028 et 8 millions de dollars destinés à la réalisation de 400 forages d’eau potable. La Banque d’investissement et de développement de la CEDEAO prévoit également 310 millions de dollars pour six projets prioritaires, tandis que le Groupe de la Banque islamique de développement envisage un financement de 200 millions de dollars, sous réserve des étapes préparatoires nécessaires. La coopération britannique constitue également une perspective importante. À l’issue du Forum sur le commerce et l’investissement entre le Royaume-Uni et l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre, Londres a annoncé le relèvement de son ambition d’investissement de 1,8 à 2,7 milliards de livres sterling, soit environ 3 milliards de dollars. Le ministre a aussi évoqué les perspectives de financement de la cité administrative par UK Export Finance. Sur le plan institutionnel, Ismaël Nabé a rappelé la confirmation, en mars 2026, de la notation souveraine de la Guinée par S&P, avec une perspective relevée à positive. Il a également annoncé l’acceptation, le 16 septembre, de la candidature guinéenne à l’adhésion au Centre de développement de l’OCDE et le relèvement, le 16 octobre, de la catégorie de risque-pays de 7 à 6. L’objectif affiché est désormais d’atteindre la catégorie 5. Au cœur de cette stratégie figure Simandou 2040, présenté comme le cadre de transformation économique du pays. Selon le ministre, ce programme comprend 122 mégaprojets représentant plus de 200 milliards de dollars d’investissements, avec l’ambition de renforcer les infrastructures, l’énergie, les compétences, les PME et la transformation locale. La territorialisation des priorités, notamment à travers les schémas régionaux d’aménagement et de développement et le Programme conjoint de développement local (PRODEL), doit rapprocher ces investissements des besoins des populations. Pour Ismaël Nabé, l’enjeu dépasse désormais la mobilisation des financements. Il s’agit de transformer les annonces en accords opérationnels, les accords en projets bancables et les investissements en résultats concrets. La poursuite des discussions avec le Fonds monétaire international et le renforcement de la planification budgétaire s’inscrivent dans cette démarche. En défendant le projet de LFR 2026, le ministre a enfin appelé à une gestion rigoureuse des ressources publiques, à la maîtrise des dépenses et à une meilleure efficacité de l’investissement. Le défi, a-t-il rappelé en substance, consiste à faire de chaque franc guinéen et de chaque dollar mobilisé un levier de développement mesurable pour les populations.

items.title: Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old
items.description: By Emmauel Okogba The Delta State Police Command has arrested a 28-year-old school bus driver, Onome Lucky Ughagha, over the alleged kidnapping and sexual assault of a 14-year-old female student in Sapele. The suspect was also accused of demanding and collecting ₦503,000 from the victim’s father as ransom before abandoning the girl along Oton Road, Sapele. The police said the incident was reported at the Sapele Area Command on October 20, 2026, by the victim’s father, who alleged that the suspect abducted his daughter while she was preparing to leave for school. According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, the suspect allegedly contacted the girl’s father, demanded ₦503,000 and threatened to kill the minor if the money was not paid. The statement said the victim was abandoned along Oton Road after the ransom was paid and subsequently reunited with her family in a traumatised condition, with indications that she had been sexually assaulted. Following the report, operatives of the Sapele Area Command commenced investigations, while the victim was taken to a medical facility for examination and treatment. The police added that the school principal and vice principal were invited for questioning as efforts intensified to apprehend the suspect, who had allegedly abandoned the school bus and fled. Edafe said the suspect was eventually arrested on October 23 at his hideout in the Ajimele area of Sapele following intelligence-led operations. “During preliminary interrogation, he reportedly confessed to his involvement in the crime,” the statement said. The police disclosed that arrangements were underway to transfer the suspect to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Asaba for further investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Delta State, CP Samuel Erale, condemned the incident and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children from violence and exploitation. He assured that the investigation would be thorough and that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The commissioner also urged school authorities, parents and transport operators to strengthen measures to protect children, stressing that the safety of every child entrusted to their care must remain a priority. The post Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La France, nouveau «malade de l’Europe» : les finances publiques et les tensions sociales inquiètent
items.description: Dans un article publie le 26 octobre, le media americain Politico designe la France comme le nouveau « malade de l'Europe ». Autrefois appliquee a l'Empire ottoman en declin, l'expression traduit les inquietudes suscitees par l'accumulation des fragilites economiques et sociales francaises. Selon le media, la deuxieme economie de l'Union europeenne est prise dans un cercle vicieux : les problemes budgetaires aggravent le mecontentement social, tandis que les manifestations compliquent les tentatives du gouvernement de retablir les finances publiques. La dette publique francaise depasse 3 500 milliards d'euros. Malgre les engagements pris aupres de ses partenaires europeens, Paris peine a reduire son deficit, alors que la faible croissance et les difficultes liees aux retraites alimentent les craintes des investisseurs. Le 22 octobre, le rendement des obligations francaises a dix ans a atteint 5,14 %, son plus haut niveau depuis 2002, selon Politico . « La France est au bord d'une crise financiere. Nous devons envoyer un signal aux marches », a mis en garde l'ancien Premier ministre Michel Barnier, cite par Politico . Le gouvernement du Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu prevoit 43 milliards d'euros d'economies dans son projet de budget pour 2027. Mais les autorites font deja face a une forte contestation sociale, ce qui limite leurs possibilites de reduire davantage les depenses. Une contestation sociale persistante Depuis septembre, les manifestations se multiplient dans le pays. Les protestataires denoncent la hausse du coût de la vie et reclament notamment de meilleurs salaires pour les enseignants ainsi que la renovation des etablissements scolaires. Selon le ministere francais de l'Interieur, 410 000 personnes ont manifeste le 24 octobre , contre 550 000 une semaine auparavant. Plusieurs rassemblements ont ete marques par des affrontements avec les forces de l'ordre. Les mobilisations accentuent la pression sur un gouvernement confronte a la fois aux exigences des marches financiers et aux revendications sociales. Aux tensions s'ajoute l'incertitude entourant la presidentielle de 2027. D'apres la publication, les investisseurs s'inquietent du coût des propositions de Marine Le Pen et de Jean-Luc Melenchon visant a abaisser l'âge de depart a la retraite, des mesures qui necessiteraient plusieurs milliards d'euros supplementaires. Les engagements budgetaires de Paris mis en cause La situation francaise rappelle a plusieurs responsables europeens la crise de la dette de 2011 en Italie, qui avait conduit au remplacement du Premier ministre italien Silvio Berlusconi par Mario Monti. Interroge par Politico , Mario Monti a averti que les difficultes financieres pouvaient s'aggraver rapidement. Mario Monti estime que la France a longtemps utilise son influence politique et economique pour s'affranchir des regles budgetaires de l'Union europeenne. L'ancien ministre francais de l'economie eric Lombard a lui-meme reconnu aupres du media que Paris n'avait pas tenu ses engagements concernant le redressement des finances publiques. Les responsables et diplomates consultes par le media n'envisagent toutefois pas, a ce stade, une crise comparable a celle de la Grece en 2015, lorsque le pays peinait a honorer ses obligations financieres. Ils redoutent plutot un scenario similaire a celui de l'Italie en 2011, avec un risque de repercussions sur d'autres economies europeennes.

items.title: Okyeame Kwame urges President Mahama, Jane Naana to honour Ghana’s founding mothers
items.description: Ghanaian musician and cultural advocate Okyeame Kwame has appealed to President John Dramani Mahama and Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang to lead a national campaign to recognise women who contributed to Ghana’s independence and nation-building. In an open letter dated Wednesday, 21st October 2026, Okyeame Kwame proposed four interventions to honour Ghana’s founding mothers, including reforms to history education, a national recognition programme, initiatives to empower women and girls, and public art commemorating their contributions. Addressing the President and the Vice President, he said they were well positioned to lead the initiative, citing the historic decision by Mr Mahama to select a woman as his running mate, who subsequently became Vice President. “I write to you (Your Excellency John Dramani Mahama and Your Excellency Mrs. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang) because I believe that in this material moment, you are the best-positioned duo with the will to lead the charge to empower women in Ghana,” he wrote. Okyeame Kwame argued that women played significant roles in Ghana’s independence struggle but their contributions have received less recognition than those of their male counterparts. “Ghana’s freedom was not won by men alone. Women organised communities, financed political movements, challenged colonial authority, communicated ideas of freedom, and helped shape our institutions and national identity,” he stated. He warned that the underrepresentation of women in the country’s historical narrative has implications beyond recognition, affecting gender equality, national development and the aspirations of future generations. As part of his Ayekoo (Big Up) campaign, the musician highlighted five women whose contributions he believes deserve greater recognition: Susanna Al-Hassan, Rebecca Naa Dedei Aryeetey, popularly known as Dedei Ashikishan, Theodosia Salome Okoh, Mabel Dove Danquah and Ama Nkrumah. He described Susanna Al-Hassan as a pioneering public servant who served in ministerial roles and contributed to education and social welfare; Rebecca Naa Dedei Aryeetey was a businesswoman whose resources and influence supported the independence movement. Theodosia Salome Okoh designed Ghana’s national flag, while Mabel Dove Danquah was a pioneering journalist, writer and political figure elected to the Gold Coast Legislative Assembly in 1954. Ama Nkrumah, he said, was a political activist and organiser whose work demonstrated the importance of grassroots mobilisation. He stressed that the women did not represent an exhaustive list, adding that Hannah Kudjoe, Oforiwaa Tagoe and other women who contributed to independence and early nationhood should also be recognised. Okyeame Kwame acknowledged existing efforts to honour distinguished women, including naming public facilities after them, but called for a broader national programme. He said the proposal was not intended to diminish the contributions of Ghana’s founding fathers, but to provide a fuller account of the country’s history. Among his recommendations is a review of the history curriculum by the Ministry of Education, the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), the Ghana Education Service and historical experts to ensure women’s contributions are taught accurately and consistently. He also proposed establishing a National Founding Mothers Recognition Programme to coordinate historians, educators, women’s organisations, traditional authorities, museums and local assemblies in documenting women’s contributions, verifying historical records and developing exhibitions and educational resources. The programme, he said, should adopt a transparent, evidence-based approach to selecting women for recognition, ensuring that the process is not determined by political affiliation or popularity. The musician further called for greater access to mentorship, leadership development, science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education, technical and vocational training, financial literacy and enterprise support for women and girls. He recommended that the initiative have measurable objectives, adequate funding and periodic public reporting. He also suggested commissioning historically informed murals and graffiti on suitable bridges and other public spaces, while naming selected roundabouts and new infrastructure after women whose contributions have helped shape Ghana. Okyeame urged the President’s Office to designate a lead institution to coordinate the proposals and make recognition of the founding mothers a lasting national commitment. “Let us honour the women who helped make Ghana possible by remembering their contributions and creating conditions in which the next generation of Ghanaian women can help shape the country’s future,” he wrote. Okyeame Kwame’s ‘Big Up’ song which features Jah Lead is now available on various streaming platforms.

items.title: Afreximbank records net income growth of 24% to US$813.5m; assets and contingencies exceed US$54.1bn
items.description: African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) and its subsidiaries (the “Group”) delivered a satisfactory financial performance for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, demonstrating resilient growth, sound asset quality and continued support for trade and economic development across Africa and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM). Net income rose by 24% to US$813.5 million, compared with US$654.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, driven by growth in lending activities, improved interest income and disciplined cost management, despite a challenging global operating environment. The Group’s total assets and contingencies increased by 12% to US$54.1 billion, from US$48.5 billion in 2025. This growth was underpinned by an expansion of the Bank’s lending portfolio, with net loans and advances increasing by 8% to US$36.2 billion, compared to US$33.5 billion at year-end 2025. Gross income increased to US$2.7 billion in nine months of 2026, up 11% from the prior period, supported by continued balance sheet growth and strong earnings generation. This performance was largely driven by a 9.1% increase in interest income to US$2.4 billion, from US$2.2 billion in nine months of 2025, underpinned by growth in average loan balances, which increased from US$28.9 billion in nine months of 2025 to US$34.8 billion in nine months of 2026, reflecting sustained demand for trade and project financing across the Bank’s member countries. Net interest income also strengthened by 15% to US$1.5 billion. Fees and commission income from unfunded business activities, including guarantees, letters of credit and advisory services, increased to US$136.9 million, from US$117.2 million in the prior-year period. The Group maintained strong operational efficiency, with its cost-to-income ratio improving to 20%, compared with 21% for the nine months ended September 2025, remaining comfortably below the Bank’s strategic ceiling of 30%. Return on average shareholders’ equity (ROAE) remained robust at 12%, while return on average assets (ROAA) improved to 2.48%, from 2.34% compared to the nine months of 2025. Asset quality remained sound, with the non-performing loans (NPL) ratio at 2.48%, compared with 2.43% as at 31 December 2025. Provisions for expected credit losses amounted to US$537.6 million, compared with US$481.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025. The Group’s liquidity position remained strong, with liquid assets totalling US$6.1 billion, representing 13% of total assets, compared with 15% at the end of 2025. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 22%, compared with 23% at the end of 2025, underscoring the resilience of the Bank’s balance sheet and alignment with its long-term capital management objectives. Shareholders’ funds increased to US$9.0 billion, from US$8.4 billion at the end of 2025, supported by internally generated profits and US$195.2 million in new equity contributions under the Bank’s General Capital Increase programme. Commenting on the results, Denys Denya, Afreximbank’s Senior Executive Vice President, said, “This performance underscores Afreximbank’s ability to deliver strong and sustainable performance while continuing to fulfil its development mandate across Africa and the Caribbean. Our expanded lending portfolio, robust profitability and strong capital position demonstrate the effectiveness of our strategy and the growing relevance of our interventions across our target markets. As global economic and geopolitical uncertainties persist, Afreximbank remains committed to providing the financing, trade facilitation and strategic investments needed to strengthen regional value chains, support industrialisation and accelerate the continent’s economic transformation.” During the period, Afreximbank further strengthened its access to international debt capital markets, successfully completing a US$1.5 billion dual-tranche bond issuance in July 2026. The transaction comprised US$750 million in 5.5-year notes and US$750 million in 10-year notes and was approximately two times oversubscribed. As a result, debt securities in issue increased to US$4.4 billion, from US$3.4 billion at the end of 2025, further supporting the diversification of the Group’s funding base. The Bank continued to demonstrate its countercyclical role in response to geopolitical and economic disruptions. Its US$10 billion Gulf Crisis Response Programme was established to provide critical liquidity support, facilitate trade and payment flows, and help member countries maintain access to essential imports, including energy products, fertilisers, food and other strategic commodities. In line with its commitment to transformative development, the Group’s high-impact investments also increased by 23% to US$1.6 billion, from US$1.3 billion at the end of 2025, supporting strategic development projects that advance industrialisation, trade competitiveness and economic resilience.

items.title: Maroc : la Marine royale expulse des bateaux de pêche mauritaniens et sénégalais au large de Lagouira
items.description: Deux patrouilleurs et plusieurs vedettes de la Marine royale marocaine ont expulse, le 25 octobre, des bateaux de peche mauritaniens et senegalais des eaux au large de Lagouira, localite aujourd'hui abandonnee, situee sur une peninsule a l'extreme sud du Sahara occidental, territoire conteste. Citee par la presse marocaine, une source proche du dossier a indique que « l'intervention s'est deroulee sans incident », precisant que « les pecheurs ont quitte les eaux marocaines sans opposer une quelconque resistance ». Un episode similaire s'etait produit en avril dernier, lorsque la Marine royale avait expulse des bateaux de peche mauritaniens au large de Lagouira. La question des frontieres meridionales du Sahara occidental alimente les discussions entre Rabat et Nouakchott. Un rapport du secretaire general des Nations unies, António Guterres, remis au Conseil de securite le 1er octobre, fait etat d'une proposition mauritanienne visant a creer une commission chargee de clarifier, par consensus, les « frontieres internationales definitives et permanentes du territoire conteste ». Cette proposition avait ete presentee par le chef de la diplomatie mauritanienne, Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, lors d'une reunion tenue les 8 et 9 fevrier 2026 a l'ambassade americaine a Madrid. La demarche de Nouakchott vise notamment a obtenir des clarifications sur les delimitations territoriales et a prevenir d'eventuels differends. Le 18 octobre, plusieurs medias ont evoque une possible revendication mauritanienne sur Lagouira, en echange d'une reconnaissance de la souverainete marocaine sur les provinces du Sud. Cette information a toutefois ete dementie le 21 octobre par le porte-parole du gouvernement mauritanien, Mohamed Ould Bebana, qui a precise que la demarche de Nouakchott visait a eviter toute « ambiguïte pouvant entraîner des consequences securitaires, juridiques ou economiques ». En 2020, le Parlement marocain a adopte deux lois relatives a la delimitation des espaces maritimes du Royaume, incluant les cotes du Sahara occidental jusqu'a Lagouira. Cette localite se trouve sur la meme peninsule que Nouadhibou, capitale economique de la Mauritanie.

items.title: Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana invests in new Hilux assembly
items.description: Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana has launched the ninth-generation Hilux and the new Land Cruiser FJ, with fresh investment in local assembly operations expected to support the company’s market expansion and contribute to the development of Ghana’s automotive industry. Speaking at the launch, Head of Sales Operations at Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana, Andrew Lamptey, says the company has invested in new equipment and workforce training to facilitate the assembly of the latest Hilux model in Ghana. He added that the new model required additional investment because the equipment used for the previous generation could not be used for the latest version. “We’ve been assembling the Hilux in Ghana over the past four or five years. And this is the confidence we have in the Ghanaian economy. Over the years, we’ve contributed so much to the Ghanaian industry. We’ve invested a lot in ensuring that we are able to assemble this particular new brand.” he said. Mr Lamptey says developing local component manufacturing could further expand the industry’s contribution to employment and economic growth. “For the moment, a lot of the assemblers are importing most of the components. But the idea is to be able to develop the industry to a point where we’ll be able to manufacture some of the components locally,” he said. He added that building local capacity could create jobs and support exports, noting that “the main goal is to be able to have a lot of component manufacturers.” National Sales and Marketing Manager at Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana, Jerry Mensan, says the launch also forms part of the company’s strategy to increase market share while improving mobility and creating employment opportunities. “Our core reason for bringing these products onto the market is to aid mobility in Ghana. Automobile mobility is part of our core. Of course, we are a business entity. And definitely market share is also a priority for us. Once we invest, we would want to get something out.” he said. Mr Mensan said the company’s local assembly operations were contributing to employment, with Ghanaians accounting for nearly all its workforce. He added that local assembly does not compromise the company’s quality standards. “About 99.9% of employees there within Toyota Ghana are all Ghanaians. The standards are not compromised although they are produced here from Ghana. We maintain the same standards that Toyota keeps way back in any of the assembly plants,” he said. Mr Lamptey said the new Hilux also incorporates customer feedback, while Toyota’s vehicles are designed with features suited to Ghana’s road conditions. The company says developing local component suppliers will be critical to expanding the automotive value chain beyond assembly, creating more jobs and positioning Ghana to benefit from future vehicle exports.

items.title: Nuit des champions AJSB : 27 athlètes récompensés dans 25 disciplines sportives
items.description: L’Association des journalistes sportifs du Burkina (AJSB) a organisé, le 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la 31ᵉ édition de la Nuit des champions. À cette occasion, 27 athlètes issus de 25 disciplines sportives ont été récompensés pour leurs performances au cours de la saison 2025-2026. La cérémonie a également été marquée par la distinction de personnalités ayant contribué au développement du sport burkinabè. De l’athlétisme au football, en passant par le basketball, le handball et le karaté-do, les meilleurs sportifs de la saison ont reçu leurs trophées des mains des personnalités présentes. Au-delà de la récompense des performances individuelles, cette édition a mis en lumière des acteurs engagés dans la promotion du sport au Burkina Faso. Trois personnalités ont été distinguées pour leur contribution à l’essor du sport au cours de la saison. Il s’agit du ministre de la Construction de la patrie, Mikaïlou Sidibé, du président de la Fédération burkinabè de handball et de celui de la Fédération burkinabè de hockey sur gazon. Pour Boubakar Sanfo, président de la Fédération burkinabè de handball, cette distinction dépasse sa personne et honore toute une discipline. « Je pense que ce trophée me dépasse, parce que je dirais que c’est une fédération qui a été honorée, c’est une discipline même qui a été honorée », a-t-il déclaré. L’AJSB saluée pour 31 ans de valorisation du sport La ministre chargée des Sports, Annick Pikbougoum Zingué/Ouattara, a félicité l’AJSB pour la continuité de cette initiative, qui met chaque année les performances sportives à l’honneur. « Grand merci et surtout félicitations à l’AJSB d’avoir tenu pendant 31 ans pour magnifier chaque année les meilleurs sportifs de notre pays » , a-t-elle souligné. De son côté, le secrétaire général du Gouvernement, Ousmane Ouattara, a rappelé la place du sport dans la vision du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, notamment en matière de croissance et d’inclusion sociale . « Toutes les initiatives qui vont dans ce sens-là ne peuvent que rencontrer l’accompagnement des autorités que nous sommes. L’année prochaine, nous allons encore être là pour les soutenir », a-t-il signifié. Un hommage aux efforts des athlètes Le président de l’AJSB, Ibrahima Diallo, a rendu hommage aux sportifs pour les efforts consentis tout au long de la saison. Derrière les performances célébrées, a-t-il rappelé, se trouvent des heures d’entraînement, des sacrifices et une détermination constante. « Derrière chaque médaille, chaque victoire, chaque record, il y a des heures de travail, des sacrifices, parfois des blessures et des doutes, mais surtout cette volonté de ne jamais renoncer » , a-t-il insisté. Pour le président de l’AJSB, le rôle des journalistes sportifs ne se limite pas à relayer les résultats des compétitions. Il consiste également à raconter les parcours des sportifs, à défendre l’éthique et à accompagner toutes les disciplines. À travers cette 31ᵉ édition de la Nuit des champions, l’AJSB réaffirme ainsi sa volonté de promouvoir le mérite sportif et de valoriser les acteurs qui contribuent au rayonnement du sport burkinabè. Faso7 L’article Nuit des champions AJSB : 27 athlètes récompensés dans 25 disciplines sportives est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Vodza Iron Breakers: You have given Keta a reason to stand tall
items.description: There are victories whose meaning travels far beyond the final whistle. They enter our homes, bring old friends together and give an entire community something to celebrate. Vodza Iron Breakers have given us such a victory. Their emphatic 4–1 win in the beach soccer final deserves a special tribute. To the players, technical team, management and supporters: you carried the name of Vodza with distinction and gave Keta a powerful reason to stand tall. A scoreline records the goals. It cannot fully capture the work that made them possible: the training, the corrections, the discipline and the willingness to keep pursuing a shared ambition. On the day that mattered, the Iron Breakers delivered. Four goals in a final. A trophy secured. A community made proud. For those of us who call this coast home, the achievement has a special resonance. Our beaches are part of our identity, our livelihoods and our everyday lives. To see our young people turn that familiar setting into a stage for sporting excellence is deeply moving. They have shown what can emerge when talent meets organisation, commitment and belief. Special recognition must go to Joshua Mawuli Kukuia and the entire management of Vodza Iron Breakers. Thank you for everything you have done to support this team and bring it to this proud moment. Behind a successful team are people who keep showing up long before the applause begins. Their work continues between competitions, away from the cameras and beyond the excitement of match day. It takes patience to build a team, commitment to sustain it and belief to keep others focused on what they can achieve together. Joshua Mawuli Kukuia and the management deserve our gratitude for that dedication. This victory belongs to them too. As we applaud the players who delivered on the sand, let us also honour those whose efforts helped make that performance possible. On Saturday, October 17, 2026, the team presented their trophy to me. It was a privilege to receive them and share in their joy. Looking at that cup, I thought about everyone whose contribution stood behind it: the players, the coaches, Joshua and his fellow management members, and the supporters who stayed with the team. Every one of them deserves a place in this celebration. During the visit, the team’s Chief Executive Officer invited me to serve as patron. I accepted with gratitude and a strong sense of responsibility. The team had already given us a reason to believe. Accepting that invitation means helping to sustain the work that brought them this far. And we must give these champions more than a moment of applause. Too often, a team wins, congratulations pour in and attention quickly moves elsewhere. Yet the next training session still has to happen. Players still need equipment, preparation, care and opportunities to improve. Management still has to plan for the next competition. If we value this achievement, our support must reach those everyday needs. Businesses, institutions, community leaders and individuals can help build a dependable foundation beneath the team. Consistent backing would allow the players, technical team and management to prepare with greater confidence and pursue even higher ambitions. The Iron Breakers have demonstrated the talent. We should help create the conditions in which that talent can keep growing. Their victory also speaks to the young person watching from the touchline and wondering how far their own ability might take them. Here is an achievement close enough to touch. Here are players carrying a familiar community’s name and succeeding together. That example matters. It gives ambition a local address. To the players: enjoy the honour you have earned. Then protect it through your conduct, discipline and preparation. Young people will watch how you train, how you treat one another and how you respond when the next challenge comes. To Joshua Mawuli Kukuia and the entire management: accept our heartfelt appreciation. Your contribution deserves to be remembered whenever the story of this victory is told. May this success strengthen your resolve and attract the support needed to carry the team further. To the coaches and technical team: thank you for preparing these champions. To the supporters: your loyalty is part of the club’s strength. Keep showing up. And to Vodza and Keta: let us celebrate with the fullness of our pride and the seriousness of our support. Vodza Iron Breakers, you carried our name into the final and brought a trophy home. You have added a proud chapter to our community’s story. May the children who watched you lift that cup one day tell their own stories of achievement and remember that you helped them believe it was possible. Congratulations, champions. You have honoured Vodza. You have honoured Keta. Now let us help you go further.

items.title: Présidentielle au Brésil : Lula décroche un quatrième mandat
items.description: Lula a ete reelu pour un quatrieme mandat presidentiel a la tete du Bresil, le 25 octobre, avec 51,79 % des voix contre 48,21 % pour son adversaire, le senateur Flávio Bolsonaro, fils de l'ex-president Jair Bolsonaro (2019-2022), condamne pour tentative de coup d'etat, qui etait arrive en tete au premier tour. Une victoire qui a cree la surprise, dans la mesure ou, depuis la fin de la dictature militaire, jamais un candidat arrive en deuxieme position au premier tour n'etait parvenu a l'emporter au second. Les Bresiliens « sont alles voter parce que nous avons reussi a les convaincre que le vote etait tres important pour garantir la democratie », a lance Lula a São Paulo, devant une foule euphorique. Flávio Bolsonaro : tel pere, tel fils ? De son cote, Flávio Bolsonaro a annonce son intention de faire annuler le scrutin, estimant qu'il etait « impossible de reconnaître les elections ». « Beaucoup de choses restent a eclaircir », a-t-il ajoute, au regard de la prolongation de deux heures des votes decidee par un juge de la Cour supreme en reponse a des requetes des deux camps . a la veille de ses 81 ans, l'ancien metallurgiste devra composer avec des bolsonaristes en force au Congres national. Lors des elections generales du 4 octobre, ceux-ci ont obtenu un nombre inedit de sieges a la Chambre des deputes depuis la promulgation de la Constitution de 1988. Ils ont egalement renforce leur presence au Senat, ou Michelle Bolsonaro, epouse de l'ancien president, et Carlos Bolsonaro, son deuxieme fils, ont chacun remporte un siege.

items.title: St. Catherine Monastery’s land ownership lawsuits adjourned after archbishop backs Egypt-Greece deal
items.description: St. Catherine’s Monastery’s archbishop said on Saturday that he intends to sign an agreement with the Egyptian government that would organize the religious community’s relationship to the monastery and surrounding lands where they have based their spiritual life for over 1,400 years. Egypt’s government had put forward a draft proposal in July that would consolidate ownership of the monastery and surrounding lands in the hands of the Egyptian state for the first time, following decades of dispute over the status of the religious sanctuary in South Sinai, which has effectively been independent of state and legal frameworks, since its history at the site predates these frameworks’ jurisdiction. The dispute had escalated when the Ismailia Court of Appeals issued a 2025 ruling establishing the state’s ownership of the monastery lands, granting the monastery’s usufruct rights to occupy and manage a majority of the property but ordering the expulsion of the monastery’s then-archbishop from a portion of the lands on the grounds that he had seized them unlawfully. The ruling precipitated a series of competing claims to the monastery and its lands and a crisis over the monastery’s leadership. Those competing claims are poised for resolution following the archbishop’s indication over the weekend that he would agree to the government’s proposal, although the former archbishop voiced condemnation for the agreement on Saturday, claiming the religious community is being pressured to accept. With Symeon Papadopoulos, the archbishop of Sinai, Pharan and Raitho, stating that he intends to sign an agreement with the Egyptian government that would bring an end to the pending legal proceedings and disputes over the monastery’s status, a parallel legal process that sought to challenge the court ruling was postponed on Sunday by the Ismailia Court of Appeals. While the 2025 ruling had upheld the government’s ownership of the monastery and surrounding lands, the court was still reviewing the monastery’s ongoing challenge to the ruling in favor of the case’s complainants: the South Sinai Governorate, the antiquities minister and the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency’s head. The court, sitting in the Tor circuit and presided over by judge Alaa Abdel Razeq, nevertheless adjourned the cases until December 27, citing the need for the parties to establish in the case files the legal capacity of the person running the monastery’s affairs. Papadopoulos has said he will arrange a date to sign the agreement with the monks and the Egyptian government “as soon as his health permits.” The archbishop’s announcement was welcomed with relief from both the Egyptian and Greek governments. In a statement published on Saturday, the Foreign Ministry said it had received a letter from Papadopoulos confirming he would sign the contract concerning the monastery and the surrounding lands “once a date for the [signing] ceremony is set.” The statement also said the agreement upholds the Ismailia Court of Appeals ruling “in full compliance with relevant national legislation, bringing all legal proceedings to an end.” Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis, meanwhile, thanked Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and Foreign Minister Badr Abdel Atty for what he described as their role in making the agreement possible. In a statement, Gerapetritis said the agreement “ensures, in perpetuity, the preservation of the Monastery’s religious character and that of its ecclesiastical properties, as well as the continuity of the Monastery through the granting of long-term residence permits to its monks.” The monastery’s lawyer, Fathy Ragheb, however, told Mada Masr that legal proceedings are still pending before the Court of Cassation and the Court of Appeals, with no final rulings so far. Ragheb asked for more time to consult with officials responsible for the monastery before providing further comment on the fate of these cases. Mada Masr also attempted to reach representatives of the monastery for comment but received no response as of time of publication. Former Archbishop Damianos’s position stood in even starker contrast to the welcome from Egyptian and Greek state officials. Damianos accused the Greek government, represented by the prime and foreign ministers, of exerting “unbearable” pressure on the monks in recent days to force them to sign what he described as a “shameful and unacceptable” settlement with the Egyptian state. “I am sure that my brothers will not open the back door for the fall of our Holy Monastery,” he added. Damianos also said that the Greek government circulated information that Egypt’s Court of Cassation could issue a final ruling on Saturday in the monastery’s case, in a bid to pressure Papadopoulos and the monks into signing the agreement proposed by the Egyptian government. Commenting on Papadopoulos’s stated intention to conclude the deal, Damianos said he was “saddened” by the decision, adding that the archbishop’s remarks neither disclosed the terms of the proposed settlement nor indicated that the other monks had consented to it, as required under the monastery’s statutes. He stressed that Papadopoulos has no right to unilaterally sign any settlement that would entail relinquishing “centuries-old historical titles.” Damianos’ 52-year leadership of the monastery came to an abrupt end in 2025. The conclusion of his leadership was precipitated by the Ismailia court ruling, which included orders to evict Damanios, in his capacity as the archbishop of St. Catherine’s Monastery at the time, from 14 disputed properties in the monastery compound in South Sinai on the grounds that he had seized the land without legal basis and carried out construction without official permits. The former archbishop claimed on Saturday that he had established an out-of-court agreement with the Egyptian government, before the 2025 court ruling, that would have seen the government explicitly and unreservedly recognize the Holy Monastery of Sinai as owner of all 71 disputed properties. The agreement was never formally signed, he said, and instead, the Ismailia Court of Appeals emerged on May 28, 2025 to affirm the Egyptian government’s ownership of the monastery’s lands, granting the monastery usufruct rights only to 57 of the total 71 properties. “The agreement was not signed because the Egyptian government, with which Mr. Gerapetritis was supposedly negotiating, allowed the decision of the Ismailia appeal court to be issued,” added Damanios. “The issue is not only legal; it is primarily political,” he continued. “No one can hide behind the decisions of Egyptian ‘justice’ in order to evade their own responsibilities.” Damanios’s response to the court ruling at the time, however, was to endorse a Greek draft law that would have handed sweeping control over the monastery’s assets to an Athens-based public authority. The move prompted a dispute over his leadership, to which he responded by sending a private guard down to throw a number of monks out of the monastery in retaliation, drawing the Patriarchate’s intervention. In a document compiled by the monks detailing their grievances and sent to Mada Masr at the time, they described Damianos’s move to locate the monastery’s assets under a legal framework in Greece without consulting them and obtaining the approval mandated by the monastery’s statutes as “the ultimate betrayal of the monastery” and a culmination of a longer breakdown in trust. The monastery’s monks voted to depose Damianos and unanimously elected Papadopoulos in his place, though there were no other nominees. An informed source told Mada Masr at the time that figures in the Greek Orthodox Church had refused to grant rival candidates ecclesiastical release to put their names forward. In July, the Egyptian government, represented by its foreign and justice ministers, presented Papadopoulos with a new agreement containing several provisions. Chief among them was recognition of the monastery as an Egyptian legal religious entity, granting the monks “religious possession” of the monastery and its religious institutions — meaning the right to reside on the grounds and practice religious rites — and allowing them to lease the surrounding gardens and land from the Egyptian government for a nominal fee over an extended period, a source close to the monastery told Mada Masr at the time on condition of anonymity. Its abbot and monks, who hold Greek, American and Lebanese nationalities, would also be granted three-year, renewable residence permits, according to the source. The foreign and justice ministers had met with Papadopoulos for more than seven hours in July, pushing him to agree to the deal in exchange for a presidential decree ratifying his election and appointment as the monastery’s head, the source said. Papadopoulos had been in a compromised position since his election in 2025, with no official recognition of his post issued by the Egyptian state, according to the source. This has left the archbishop unable to deal with the monastery’s Egyptian bank accounts or conduct transactions with state institutions in South Sinai. The source noted that while Papadopoulos holds a Greek diplomatic passport, which allows him to travel to and from Egypt for two years, the rest of the monks hold 12-month tourist visas that take three months to renew, leaving them with, in reality, only nine months of residency. The proposed arrangement would follow the precedent set by former President Anwar al-Sadat, who had appointed Damianos as archbishop and later granted him Egyptian citizenship. The Egyptian government’s proposed agreement builds off the May 2025 Ismailia court ruling , which recognized the state’s ownership of St. Catherine’s Monastery and its lands while granting the monks limited usufruct rights for religious use and possession. The ruling also placed all dealings involving the properties under the direct supervision of state authorities. The court also ruled that the monastery’s spiritual affiliation with the Greek Orthodox Church does not confer any legal privileges on it within Egypt. The Ismailia court split the disputed lands into four categories. The first covers the land on which the monastery itself is built, along with other plots that hold some churches and shrines. The monks and archbishop were granted what the court termed “religious possession” of these properties for residence and worship, while ownership remains with the state under the supervision of the Supreme Council of Antiquities. The second category comprises lands outside the monastery’s boundaries, which the court incorporated into the St. Catherine Protectorate under the supervision of the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency. The third consists of agricultural land that the court termed “expulsion lands,” ordering the monks be expelled from it on the grounds that they are occupying it by force. The fourth includes several plots with small churches and monastic facilities covered by preliminary contracts between the monastery and the local administrative unit of St. Catherine. The court ruled that these contracts did not transfer ownership but instead established reciprocal obligations. The source close to the monastery, as well as a second one, previously told Mada Masr Greece supports the Egyptian proposal, and Egyptian officials were working to pressure Papadopoulos and the rest of the monks to agree to the terms, despite what the sources said is a relinquishment of the monastery’s land ownership. They also said Egyptian government representatives put forward the new agreement in July after reaching an understanding with the Greek government. The Friends of St. Catherine’s Monastery Facebook page, which reflects the views of a number of monks, described at the time the agreement as a disastrous formula that dismantles the monastery of its rights and deprives it of its ownership. The group argued that the Egyptian and Greek governments were placing their political and economic interests above the spiritual and historical significance of one of the world’s oldest inhabited monasteries where religious rites are still held. The monastery is being sold in the market of political and economic interests in exchange for the energy agreement that Athens seeks to conclude with Cairo, the group stated. The 2025 court ruling established the state’s ownership of the area for the first time, leaving it at the mercy of the state, which can revoke its legal standing at any time, according to Stephan Dömpke, the head of World Heritage Watch, an independent organization dedicated to protecting UNESCO sites, who spoke to Mada Masr at the time of the court ruling. “Being at the mercy of the Egyptian government is what terrifies the monastery and the whole Orthodox Church,” Dömpke told Mada Masr, “especially when considering the tourism developments unfolding around them without their consent.” In 2021, the Egyptian government launched the “Great Transfiguration” project , aimed at transforming the city of St. Catherine into an international center for Abrahamite religions. Since then, large-scale construction has taken place in the city and around the monastery as part of what the government has described as a “developmental and touristic” initiative. The post St. Catherine Monastery’s land ownership lawsuits adjourned after archbishop backs Egypt-Greece deal first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: CIB Ghana, GhISP build financial institutions capacity to drive gender-smart
items.description: Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana (CIB Ghana), in partnership with the Ghana Investment Support Programme (GhISP), held a two-day workshop for the SME portfolio managers from banks across Ghana. This programme was designed specifically to support financial institutions in capacity-building and inclusive lending towards Small and Medium-sized Enterprise (SME) sector. Held on 15 th and 16 th October 2026 at CIB Ghana in Accra, the workshop brought together professionals from banks and selected Finance Houses to deepen their understanding of contemporary approaches to SME financing. Reflecting on the programme, one participant noted: “One of the challenges we face in financing SMEs is assessing businesses that may be viable but do not always have the financial records or structures we traditionally rely on for credit decisions. The workshop has given us practical approaches to look more closely at cash flows, the business model and other indicators of viability. We will take these insights back to our institution to strengthen how we assess SMEs and structure financing that better responds to their needs.” SMEs constitute an important component of Ghana’s economy, supporting employment, innovation and economic growth. However, challenges including weak financial records, inadequate governance, poor cash-flow management and limited investment readiness continue to constrain access to finance. Against this background, the workshop focused on strengthening financing opportunities and developing lending approaches that are both commercially sound and responsive to emerging sustainability and inclusion considerations. Participants were taken through practical areas including SME business models, inclusive product design, governance and risk assessment, climate risk and green SME financing, credit assessment, cash-flow-based lending, gender-smart finance and inclusive investment. The programme adopted an interactive approach combining expert presentations, practical case studies, experience sharing and group discussions, enabling participants to relate the concepts to real lending and portfolio-management situations within their institutions. The workshop forms part of a broader CIB Ghana – GhISP initiative aimed at improving the quality of SME lending, enhancing financial inclusion and encouraging financial institutions to integrate climate considerations into lending decisions. At the conclusion of the programme, participating institutions were encouraged to translate the lessons from the workshop into practical actions within their organisations, particularly in credit assessment, product development, portfolio management and engagement with SMEs. Commenting on the expected impact of the programme, Mr. Robert Dzato, CEO of CIB Ghana, stated that “Strengthening the capacity of financial institutions to adopt sound, inclusive and sustainable lending practices is essential to improving SMEs’ access to finance and supporting their long-term growth. CIB Ghana remains committed to equipping banking professionals with the knowledge and skills to make informed financing decisions that support SME development and Ghana’s economic growth.” The Accra workshop represents the first of two ecosystem workshops under the initiative, with the second scheduled to take place in Kumasi in November 2026. About CIB Ghana Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana (CIB Ghana) is the professional body for the practice of banking in Ghana, established under the Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana Act, 2019 (Act 991). The Institute’s mandate is to promote the study of banking and regulate the practice of the banking profession in Ghana. Through professional education, certification, capacity building and industry engagement, CIB Ghana supports the development of competent and ethical banking professionals and contributes to the advancement of the banking and financial services industry. For further information, contact CIB Ghana at info@cibgh.org . About GhISP The Ghana Investment Support Programme (GhISP) is a technical assistance initiative, powered by British International Investment (BII) and supported by SECO and Norfund. The programme aims to increase investment flows to underserved SMEs in Ghana, with a particular focus on gender, inclusion and climate investing. Through tailored pre- and post-investment support, GhISP helps SMEs get investment-ready and connect them to capital, supporting investments for Growth Investment Partners (GIP) Ghana and other relevant funds in Ghana. Learn more at ghisp.org or contact GhISP Communications Lead, Tine Frank at tine_frank@ghisp.org .
