Imaan, Hadi move SC against IHC order refusing to stay trial in security breach case
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Incarcerated human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, on Monday approached the Supreme Court to challenge the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial before an anti-terrorism court (ATC) in the security breach case. The case pertains to the alleged disruption of the security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on October 7. On Oct 19, the IHC took up appeals filed by Imaan and Hadi against the Oct 10 ATC order that rejected their petitions challenging the framing of charges and the inclusion of terrorism-related provisions. While issuing notices, the IHC had said it would decide how to proceed once the parties’ responses were received. Subsequently, the couple, through senior counsel Faisal Siddiqui, filed separate near-identical petitions before the SC on Monday, challenging the IHC’s Oct 19 order. The plea argued that the trial court proceeded with unprecedented haste by recording the examination-in-chief of six prosecution witnesses on Oct 10 and 14, and accepting the prosecution’s request to shift the trial to jail. The decision to conduct the trial in jail had also been challenged before the IHC, with the petition pointing out that the trial court had appointed state counsel . The petitions alleged that the ongoing trial was nothing but persecution aimed at subverting the SC’s order suspending the petitioners’ 17-year sentences in the controversial social media post case and at preventing their eventual release through an allegedly frivolous and mala fide case that had mysteriously resurfaced. Imaan’s petition argued that the IHC had “erroneously refused to exercise its discretion to grant ad interim relief to stay the criminal trial, despite multiple factual and legal reasons warranting such relief and repeated requests”. It said it was settled law that ad interim relief could not be denied in the presence of a prima facie case and where the balance of convenience favoured the petitioner, as she would otherwise suffer irreparable loss. The petition pleaded that Imaan had a clear prima facie case because recording evidence in their absence violated Section 353 (evidence to be taken in presence of accused) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), as well as their due process and fair trial rights guaranteed under the law. It further argued that the balance of convenience favoured the petitioner because delaying the trial for some time would not prejudice the prosecution. The plea claimed that the petitioner would suffer irreparable loss given the alleged gross violations of due process and fair trial principles in the proceedings, adding that it was apparent that the trial was leading to her criminal conviction. The petitioner’s liberty was at stake because of the denial of ad interim relief, the petition contended, adding that the IHC’s order was without jurisdiction, illegal and liable to be set aside. It further pointed out that the trial court had never dispensed with the petitioner’s personal attendance during the recording of evidence and that no proceedings under Section 540-A (power to summon material witness or examine person present) of the CrPC had been initiated. The trial court’s order of Oct 10 recorded that counsel had left the rostrum and the accused had left the video link. The Oct 14 order also noted that the accused had again moved away from the camera while their counsel had left the rostrum during the examination-in-chief of witnesses. Despite this, the court proceeded to record the examination-in-chief of six prosecution witnesses on the two dates. The petitions emphasised that the absence of the petitioners and their counsel was forced as a protest and had been recorded as such, but did not amount to a waiver of the right to be present during the recording of evidence. IHC hears plea against jail trial, appointment of state counsel Meanwhile, the IHC heard arguments on a petition filed by Imaan and Hadi challenging their trial at Adiala jail and the appointment of a state counsel . A division bench comprising Justice Raja Inaam Ameen Minhas and Justice Shahrukh Arjumand continued the proceedings, with advocates Riasat Ali Azad and Zainab Janjua appearing for the petitioners. During the proceedings, Advocate Azad noted that the decision to conduct the trial inside the jail had been challenged before the IHC. He contended that the accused should have been heard before such an arrangement was approved. Justice Minhas questioned the legal basis of the challenge, asking who had the authority to decide the venue of a trial and whether an accused could dictate where the proceedings should take place. In response, Azad said the petitioners were being brought before what he described as a “jail court”, effectively a cage, where access to the proceedings was restricted. He argued that the summary for conducting the jail trial had been initiated by an Islamabad superintendent of police and subsequently approved by the chief commissioner. According to him, the police officer lacked the authority to initiate such a summary, which he maintained fell within the federal government’s domain. The judge questioned whether a summary concerning a jail trial would have to be placed before the cabinet and also asked about the legal concept of an open court. Azad said he had not been heard before the decision was taken, despite the need to hear the defence. He pointed out that journalists and members of the public were not permitted to attend the proceedings inside the jail. He further submitted that the defence had requested the trial judge to pass a formal judicial order regarding the arrangement, but the judge declined, telling the lawyers to challenge the matter before the high court. The lawyer also objected to the appointment of a state counsel during the jail trial. Justice Minhas observed that the defence lawyers’ vakalatnamas (powers of attorney authorising legal representation) were still on the court record. Advocate Janjua clarified that she had initially represented the accused but subsequently withdrew her vakalatnama , explaining that travelling to Adiala jail every day was incompatible with managing her legal practice. Azad added that travelling to and from the jail took around two hours each way. When the judge again asked whether his vakalatnama remained on record, Azad said the defence had effectively been sidelined. He alleged that when he sought a single adjournment, a state counsel was appointed and the cross-examination of prosecution witnesses was conducted in his absence. Questioning the urgency of the proceedings, Azad said the first information report (FIR) had remained concealed for two years and that the accused had been arrested in the case immediately after securing bail from the SC. He further contended that although the original charges were bailable, a terrorism-related charge had subsequently been added. The counsel requested the IHC to restrain the trial court from delivering its final verdict until the petition was decided. Justice Minhas observed that the accused could also be acquitted, asking the lawyer why he was seeking such an order. Advocate Azad reiterated the request that the trial court be restrained from announcing its final verdict. After hearing the arguments, Justice Minhas remarked that the court would examine the matter. The bench did not announce a final decision on the request during the proceedings.

items.title: Tagadayat : l’armée annonce la découverte de 54 corps
items.description: © Internet Une patrouille a retrouvé 54 corps dans un campement situé au sud-est de Ménaka, selon l’état-major général des Armées. Neuf rescapés ont été évacués vers la ville pour recevoir des soins. L’état-major général des Armées a annoncé samedi 24 octobre la découverte de 54 corps dans un campement de Tagadayat, à environ 35 kilomètres au sud-est de Ménaka. La patrouille avait été envoyée dans la zone après des informations faisant état d’attaques contre des populations civiles. Les victimes ont été inhumées sur place. Neuf personnes retrouvées vivantes ont été transportées à Ménaka et confiées aux services chargés de leur prise en charge. L’armée affirme que les premiers témoignages recueillis attribuent les tueries à l’État islamique au Grand Sahara. Cette attribution constitue la version officielle communiquée par l’état-major. Les comptes rendus consultés ne font état d’aucune revendication authentifiée du groupe. Un bilan actualisé après les premières alertes L’attaque avait été signalée le dimanche 18 octobre. Le lendemain, le bureau exécutif de la communauté Idaksahak avait annoncé la mort d’au moins 48 civils à Tagadayat. Il faisait également état de blessés et de déplacements de familles vers Ménaka. Le chiffre de 54 annoncé par l’armée correspond aux corps découverts pendant les recherches sur le terrain. Il actualise le premier bilan communautaire de 48 victimes. Les deux nombres concernent la même attaque et ne doivent pas être additionnés. Les informations publiées permettent désormais de retenir plusieurs éléments précis. L’attaque remonte au 18 octobre, la découverte annoncée porte sur 54 corps, neuf rescapés ont été évacués et les recherches se sont déroulées dans un campement situé à 35 kilomètres de Ménaka. L’identité complète des victimes et la répartition entre hommes, femmes et enfants restent absentes des comptes rendus publics. Le nombre de familles ayant quitté les campements voisins n’a pas davantage été chiffré. Des habitants déplacés vers Ménaka L’état-major indique avoir renforcé les mesures de protection et facilité le déplacement vers Ménaka des habitants de campements exposés. Des patrouilles et des opérations de sécurisation se poursuivent dans le secteur. La communauté Idaksahak avait demandé une assistance urgente pour les personnes déplacées. Les besoins cités concernent l’accueil, l’alimentation, les soins et la protection des civils. Leur évaluation locale repose maintenant sur le recensement des familles arrivées à Ménaka et sur la situation des campements encore occupés. L’annonce du 24 octobre apporte ainsi un bilan officiel issu des recherches menées à Tagadayat. Elle confirme l’ampleur des pertes civiles signalées six jours auparavant et fait état de mouvements de populations vers Ménaka. Les prochains bilans des services locaux devront préciser le nombre de déplacés et l’assistance effectivement déployée.

items.title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
items.description: Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price. The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline. “I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said. Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job. The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired. David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching. – Sentimental choice – Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson. “The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports. “But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.” The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout. Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed. Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion). United, who for years bullied their rivals in the transfer market, lost out on the biggest names as they targeted a summer midfield rebuild, with Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes all choosing other clubs. United instead recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — none of whom have made a strong impression — for combined fees of about £150 million. Significant rifts have emerged in recent weeks. Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox for not doing more to strengthen Carrick’s squad. Last week captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 humbling by Champions League debutants Como. Carrick is expected to take the blame, but the route back to the top for one of the world’s biggest clubs appears tougher than ever. “It can’t just be the manager again. There has got to be consequences above that. You can’t keep letting the people pick the manager who keep getting it wrong,” said Neville. “It’s years now without a Premier League title. That will be another five or 10 before you know it because there are other clubs set up for success and Manchester United aren’t.” The post Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Redefining Africa’s Infrastructure: The role of technology in connecting infrastructure system
items.description: The asset-by-asset era is ending Infrastructure is becoming a connected system—not a collection of stand-alone assets. Roads, power, water, digital networks and logistics must increasingly work together. That shift will determine how economies scale, how reliably essential services perform and how communities thrive. PwC’s Global Infrastructure Outlook 2025-50 report anticipates that, by 2050, infrastructure will be shaped by electrification, data, automation and circular resource flows. Roads could support autonomous vehicles, dynamic pricing and wireless charging. Airports could become predictive, intermodal hubs for drones and electrified aircraft. Across sectors, intelligent systems could anticipate demand, allocate resources and lift productivity. Stop-start funding carries a long-term cost Integration demands consistency. Yet “boom-and-bust” funding cycles continue to weaken long-term planning, delivery capacity and skills—especially in capital-intensive sectors such as rail. PwC’s Rail Outlook 2050 Report points to a practical response: more consistent and predictable medium- to long-term investment planning by governments and their stakeholders. Technology is now core infrastructure There is no credible path to deeper integration without technology. PwC’s Global Data Centre Outlook 2026 – 2050 report estimates that global data-centre capital expenditure could reach US$31.6 trillion through 2050, with a plausible upside of nearly US$50 trillion if AI adoption accelerates. The opportunity extends beyond capacity. Data and AI can connect transport, energy, water and digital assets; improve real-time decisions; optimise resources; and strengthen resilience. Five moves can unlock the next wave Contract for outcomes. Make sustainability, impact, resilience and reliability central to commercial models. Innovate finance and partnerships. Public budgets cannot carry the requirement alone. Sharper risk-sharing, faster routes to bankability and stronger public-private delivery models are essential. Redesign planning and construction. Co-design, co-locate and co-optimise assets across sectors. Build with more sustainable and circular practices. Plan beyond the political cycle. Clear national and regional strategies, backed by stable regulation, can turn ambition into investable pipelines. Engage communities early—and often. Infrastructure creates value only when intended outcomes are realised by the people it serves. Every actor has a move to make Governments must create enabling regulation, transparent pipelines and credible financing frameworks. Investors must track the changing risk-return landscape and direct capital towards sectors with durable growth. Corporations must pursue cross-sector partnerships and use technology to adapt. Communities must help shape priorities and delivery. In Conclusion Africa’s infrastructure opportunity is not simply to build more. It is to connect better. Political stability, policy consistency, regulatory certainty and disciplined execution will determine whether integrated infrastructure attracts capital—and converts it into inclusive, sustained growth. Achieving this future will require leadership. Leaders must convert vision into value through clear, actionable plans. They must make difficult choices, direct scarce resources to the highest-impact projects and act with clarity and speed. They must also be prepared to adopt non-traditional models where the evidence shows they work.

items.title: Comment l’Amérique latine réagit à la victoire de Lula
items.description: Le président brésilien Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a été réélu hier, dimanche 25 octobre, pour un quatrième mandat contre Flávio Bolsonaro, le fils de l’ex-président Jair Bolsonaro, assigné à résidence après avoir été condamné à 27 ans de prison pour tentative de coup d’État. La cérémonie d’investiture aura lieu le 5 janvier 2027. À cette heure, les gouvernements de la moitié des pays de la région (16 sur 32) ont adressé leurs félicitations à Lula, et aucune réaction officielle n’a été relevée pour 13 d’entre eux. Le Costa Rica est le seul pays d’Amérique latine dont le gouvernement a « félicité le peuple brésilien d’avoir […] élu son nouveau président dans un processus démocratique et pacifique », sans toutefois nommer Lula. En Colombie, le président Abelardo de la Espriella, qui avait soutenu Flávio Bolsonaro, a reconnu la victoire de Lula sans le féliciter : « Ni Lula ne décide pour les Colombiens, ni moi pour les Brésiliens », et a évoqué de « grandes et profondes différences politiques et idéologiques » avec le président brésilien. En la campaña presidencial colombiana, el presidente Lula apoyó abiertamente a Iván Cepeda y gané yo. En la campaña brasileña, apoyé a Bolsonaro y ganó Lula. Ni Lula decide por los colombianos ni yo decido por los brasileños. ¡DECIDE LA GENTE ! Y cuando el pueblo se pronuncia en… — Abelardo De La Espriella (@ABDELAESPRIELLA) October 26, 2026 En Argentine, le gouvernement de Javier Milei n’a pas encore publié de communiqué au sujet de l’élection brésilienne, et le président n’a pas félicité Lula. En amont du scrutin, Milei avait écrit sur le réseau social X espérer que le « dernier tour de campagne sale » de Lula « n’inclue pas de voler l’élection ». Le jour du vote, il a partagé des publications accusant Lula de vouloir « voler » l’élection. – Paraliza el conteo de votos – Mete preso al Sec. de Transporte de Bahía por no permitir su fraude y acarreo – Pide al Juez Supremo (que es su amigo) que extienda el tiempo de votación – Ya sabe los resultados de la elección, pero no los publica, mientras se sigue votando pic.twitter.com/txYTBcbwC4 — El Trumpista (@ElTrumpista) October 25, 2026 Dans ses stories Instagram, Milei a partagé une image avec la légende « Lula voleur et menteur », selon le quotidien argentin Perfil . Il a également publié une image générée par l’IA le représentant aux côtés de Flávio Bolsonaro, avec une citation attribuée à ce dernier : « J’ai confiance dans le fait que le Brésil pourra se relever » Del “Lula ladrón” al mutismo : el Gobierno nacional no habla de la victoria del PT en Brasil », Perfil , 25 octobre 2026.'> 1 . La victoire de Lula, avec plus de 4 millions de voix d’avance sur Flávio Bolsonaro, interrompt la série de victoires enregistrées par des candidats proches ou alignés sur Donald Trump, depuis 2025. Mis à part au Suriname, où la candidate de gauche Jennifer Geerlings-Simons avait été élue en juillet 2025, tous les scrutins majeurs avaient débouché sur l’élection d’un dirigeant proche de Washington. La réélection de Trump, en novembre 2024, avait coïncidé avec un effet domino qu’il semble avoir au moins en partie entraîné : en plus du Pérou, l’Équateur, la Bolivie, le Chili, le Costa Rica, la Colombie et le Honduras avaient élu des présidents de droite et d’extrême droite. Sur les cinq principales économies de la région, le Brésil et le Mexique, qui représentent plus de la moitié du PIB de l’Amérique latine, sont les seuls pays dirigés par un président de gauche. L’article Comment l’Amérique latine réagit à la victoire de Lula est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl
items.description: American R&B singer Chris Brown avoided jail when sentenced by a UK court Monday after pleading guilty to a public order offence during a 2023 brawl at a London nightclub. The former boyfriend of music sensation Rihanna was handed an eight-month jail sentence suspended for a year — meaning he will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the period. Brown, 37, who was wearing a black face mask and black cap when he arrived Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, had admitted to affray during an appearance in July. “Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious. It creates an obvious risk, not merely to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others,” judge Tony Baumgartner said, handing down the sentence. Prosecutors had accused him and co-defendant Omololu Akinlolu, also a US national, of carrying out “a vicious and unprovoked attack” in a crowded nightclub “where Brown used a glass bottle as a weapon to strike the victim’s head twice”. The guilty plea avoided a trial on several other charges, including attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon, namely a bottle. Brown, who has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, had earlier denied those charges. All of the allegations relate to an incident at Tape, a private members’ club in central London, on February 19, 2023, while Brown was touring the UK. The victim was struck several times with a bottle before being pursued, punched and kicked. The singer is known for mid-2000s hits such as “Kiss, Kiss”, as well as a litany of legal troubles including a felony conviction for assaulting Rihanna in 2009. Brown rose from a local church choir in Virginia to sudden fame with his rich R&B voice before turning to rap. He was convicted of having beaten then-girlfriend Rihanna before the 2009 Grammy Awards, forcing the pop star to miss the annual gala. In 2012, Brown was involved in an altercation at a New York nightclub with members of hip hop star Drake’s entourage, during which French basketball player Tony Parker suffered an eye injury after being hit by a thrown glass bottle. Two years later, Brown pleaded guilty to assaulting a fan in Washington. Akinlolu, 40 also pleaded guilty to affray over the London incident. He was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment suspended for a year. The post US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Peter Obi demands supporter’s release, accuses Tinubu of undermining democracy
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has demanded the release of party supporter Rilwan Olawale, accusing President Bola Tinubu of undermining democracy by “encouraging and facilitating violence.” In a statement posted on X on Monday, Obi described the reported incident as part of what he called the intimidation and harassment of his supporters. He also accused President Bola Tinubu of encouraging and facilitating violence, and demanded transparency over Olawale’s reported arrest, respect for his rights and an end to what he described as politically motivated harassment. “The continued intimidation and harassment of my supporters across the country, the latest being the case of Rilwan Olawale, is disturbing and unacceptable. “President Bola Tinubu has remained a huge beneficiary of our democracy and should not brazenly be destroying it by encouraging and facilitating violence.” Obi further stated that his campaign was peaceful and issue-driven, and warned that his supporters’ restraint should not be mistaken for weakness. “We have chosen the path of peace, not violence; persuasion, not intimidation. However, nobody should mistake our civility for weakness, our restraint for fear, or our commitment to peace for an absence of resolve. We will not be intimidated into silence, nor will we abandon Nigerians who believe in a New Nigeria that is possible and will be OK.” He called for Olawale’s release and said Nigerians should be free to support the candidate of their choice. “I therefore demand transparency regarding Rilwan Olawale’s arrest, his release, respect for his rights, and an end to politically motivated harassment. No government or political party has the right to deny Nigerians the freedom to support a candidate of their choice. “We will remain peaceful but resolute. We will not resort to violence, but we will stand firmly and lawfully against every attempt to undermine our democratic rights.” According to NDC’s Lagos governorship candidate, Funso Doherty, Olawale was reportedly taken from his residence at about 1 a.m. on Sunday by men who identified themselves as Department of State Services (DSS) operatives. Doherty, in a statement on his X handle on Sunday, said he was in contact with Olawale’s family and legal counsel, who were seeking to establish what happened and gain access to him. He said: “This afternoon, reports reached me that Mr. Rilwan Olawale, a strong NDC supporter, who is also identified with the Obidient movement, was allegedly picked up by some armed men who identified themselves as operatives of the Department of State Services in the very early hours of today, Sunday 25th October.” Doherty also urged the public to remain calm while the family and legal counsel sought information about Olawale’s whereabouts. The circumstances of the reported arrest and the reason for it remained unclear in reports available on Monday. “The circumstances surrounding this situation are still unclear and there is no official confirmation of his exact whereabouts. However, we are in contact with his family as well as with legal counsel who are working to gain access to him and to establish the relevant facts. We urge the public to stay calm and avoid speculation for now while these and further steps are being taken to ascertain the facts, ensure that Mr Olawale’s rights are fully respected and that Justice is served,” he added. The post Peter Obi demands supporter’s release, accuses Tinubu of undermining democracy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Millicent Nice Apeku wins NDC Ashaiman Deputy Secretary position
items.description: Millicent Nice Apeku has been elected Deputy Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Ashaiman Constituency of the Greater Accra Region. She secured 1,362 votes in the constituency executive elections held on Saturday, October 24, to emerge ahead of three other contenders. Kpotosu-Mensah Michael placed second with 631 votes, followed by Joseph Frimpong, who polled 723 votes, while David Quami Acheampong obtained 94 votes. Five ballots were rejected, with the total votes cast recorded at 2,815. Speaking to news reporters during press engagement to show appreciation to delegates and outlining her priorities on Monday, October 26, she said her victory places her in the constituency’s leadership structure, where she is expected to support party administration, communication, coordination and the implementation of organisational decisions. Ms Apeku has built her political experience through various roles within the NDC, spanning student politics, grassroots communication and constituency-level administration, she noted. She previously served as Deputy Secretary of the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) at Takoradi Technical University. She also worked as Branch Communications Officer for the Nii Man Ward in Ashaiman, Deputy Coordinator of the Young Professional Forum in the Greater Accra Region, and a member of the NDC’s Ashaiman Constituency Executive. These roles have provided her with experience in party organisation, grassroots mobilisation and internal communication. As Deputy Secretary, Ms Apeku said she is committed to working with constituency executives and party members to strengthen the party’s internal structures and promote unity and discipline. Her priorities include encouraging greater participation by young people and women in party activities and improving administrative coordination within the constituency. Her journey from Alakple in the Volta Region to her professional role at the Tema Oil Refinery, alongside her involvement in party politics, reflects her pursuit of professional growth and leadership, she told the media. According to her, the new role marks another step in her political career as she takes on a new responsibility in the NDC’s Ashaiman Constituency leadership.

items.title: Jordan arrests three men suspected of deadly church attack after shootout
items.description: Jordanian security forces have arrested three armed men suspected of a shooting attack at a church last week that killed nine Christians and injured 34 other people, officials say. The Public Security Directorate (PSD) said the unnamed “terrorists” were located before dawn inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman. They refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and wounded all three of them, it added. No security personnel were hurt in the shootout. No group has yet claimed it was behind Friday’s attack by gunmen on a funeral at St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hmoud, which is in Karak governorate. King Abdullah II praised security forces for chasing the suspects “to the very end”. “We vowed the terrorists would not escape punishment, and no proponent of dark ideologies that divide Jordanians will be tolerated,” he wrote on X. “We pray that the martyrs’ souls rest in peace and wish the injured a speedy recovery. May God protect and watch over Jordan and its people.” Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities would hold to account anyone involved in the attack and were “examining every factor that leads youth toward extremism”. Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom. Verified CCTV footage from Friday showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George’s church. A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes. One man who was at the church told BBC Arabic that the attack lasted around 15 minutes. “Some [people at the funeral] were taking cover, some were cradling the dead, others were holding their sons close, some were grabbing their children and fleeing, while others were holding onto their friends who were with them at the church,” Khalid al-Mdanat said. He added that the gunmen fled in a pick-up truck, “firing as they went”. On Sunday, the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem, Theophilos III, visited wounded survivors of the attack, which he condemned as a “vile, cowardly, and bloody act”. He also led the funeral at St George’s of eight of the victims – Dr Maher Zureiqat, Ihab al-Halsa, Dr Fadi al-Halsa, Dr Khaled al-Halsa, Dr Asim al-Burqan, Alaa al-Masarwa, Marwan Khaitan and Mazen al-Qassous – which was attended by thousands of people. The ninth victim, Dr Mohammed al-Qassous, was laid to rest near Amman on Monday.

items.title: Shirley Frimpong-Manso defends foreign involvement in ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ documentary
items.description: Ghanaian filmmaker Shirley Frimpong-Manso has defended the involvement of foreign producers in The Eyes of Ghana , describing criticism of their participation as misplaced. Speaking to arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie on Showbiz A-Z on Joy FM , Shirley said arguments that the involvement of the Obamas, IShowSpeed and other foreign film companies in the documentary was inappropriate overlooked the people responsible for developing and executing the project. “IShowSpeed coming in would have basically been for the publicity. It doesn’t take away from the people who actually thought the thing and executed it. Somebody said the most expensive thing about film is your time. It’s the time you put in. It’s the ideas behind it. And it’s the people who actually make the move,” she noted. She added that many world-class films are funded by other people, arguing that there was nothing wrong with a Ghanaian-themed film receiving foreign funding. Shirley said she was surprised that some people were sensationalising the involvement of foreigners, questioning how Ghanaians could have allowed others to make a film about them. “First off it’s art. And especially when you have been mentioned in something, you take advantage of it and you own it. What is wrong if somebody even did it, and we had no Ghanaians in it. If it’s shedding positive light on our history, you embrace it and you go with it. Argentinians everywhere, no matter what Messi is doing, for them it’s Argentina. And you claim it and you own it and that’s how it’s supposed to be,” she said. The Eyes of Ghana is a documentary directed by two-time Academy Award-winning filmmaker Ben Proudfoot. It follows 93-year-old Ghanaian cinematographer Rev. Dr Chris Tsui Hesse, who served as the personal cameraman to Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, and explores his efforts to preserve more than 1,000 reels of historical footage documenting Ghana’s independence and the wider African liberation movement. The film is produced by a team that includes Proudfoot, Ghanaian producers Nana Adwoa Frimpong and Anita Afonu, Moses Bwayo, Brandon Somerhalder, Ethan Lewis, Vinnie Malhotra and American streamer IShowSpeed, whose real name is Darren Watkins Jr. Former United States President Barack Obama and former First Lady Michelle Obama are executive producers through their production company, Higher Ground. Other Ghanaian contributors include co-producers Yaw Amponsah Apenteng and Justice Baidoo, assistant editor Annabelle Toe, and musician Dela Botri, who contributed as a featured instrumentalist. The documentary premiered at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival and has since received international recognition. In Ghana, it was screened at the University of Media, Arts and Communication’s Institute of Film and Television in Accra in April 2026. Another free screening is scheduled for Saturday, 31st October 2026, at 6.30 pm at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park in Accra, with registration required. The film is also scheduled for a one-night cinema release in the United States and Canada on Wednesday, 28th October 2026. Shirley Frimpong-Manso is one of Ghana’s established film directors, writers and producers. Through Sparrow Productions, she has made films including The Perfect Picture , A Sting in a Tale , Adams Apples , 6 Hours to Christmas , Contract , Potomanto , Love or Something Like That , Rebecca and Potato Potahto . Her work has earned her industry recognition, including the Best Director award at the Africa Movie Academy Awards and other prestigious awards at the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Her latest comedy, Agency for the Dead , is scheduled to open in Ghanaian cinemas on Friday, 30th October 2026. The film draws on Ghanaian folklore and childhood ghost stories, offering a comic take on supernatural beliefs. Its cast includes Anita Erskine, David Dontoh, George Quaye, Joselyn Dumas, Mawuli Gavor, Omari Dwamena, Rhoda Ampene and Yvonne Okoro.

items.title: Affaire Kamel Daoud : sa femme sort du silence
items.description: Mise en cause dans l’affaire du roman “Houris”, la femme de Kamel Daoud sort du silence. Aicha Dahdouh s’est exprimée dans un communiqué transmis dimanche 25 octobre à l’AFP, alors que le tribunal d’Oran devrait rendre son verdict ce mardi. Tout en clamant son innocence, la femme se démarque des positions de l’écrivain sur l'Algérie, l'islam et la Palestine. Aïcha Dahdouh, psychiatre, est soupçonnée d'avoir divulgué un secret médical en racontant l’histoire d’une de ses patientes à son mari qui l’a mise en roman. Le roman en question, “Houris”, a remporté le prix Goncourt 2024. Aicha Dahdouh, femme de Kamel Daoud : “Je suis innocente” Saada Arbane, une rescapée d’un attentat terroriste en Algérie dans les années 1990, a reconnu sa propre histoire à travers le personnage principal de l’œuvre et a saisi la justice. Mme Arbane a soutenu que la seule personne qui pouvait divulguer à Kamel Daoud les détails de son drame c'est sa femme Aicha Dahdouh, qui n’est autre que la psychiatre qui la suivait. “Je suis innocente. Je n'ai pas divulgué de secret médical. Je n'ai pas volé de dossier », a indiqué la femme de l’écrivain dans son communiqué transmis à l’AFP. “Le secret médical est l'un des fondements de l'éthique médicale, et je lui ai toujours été fidèle », s’est-elle défendue. “Je ne partage pas ses positions sur l'Algérie, l'islam et la Palestine” S’agissant du procès de son mari en Algérie, dans lequel elle est également poursuivie, Aicha Dahdouh a indiqué qu'elle aurait souhaité s’y présenter mais, explique-t-elle, elle a été empêchée par « le retentissement des positions de Kamel Daoud et une situation familiale douloureuse ». La femme de Kamel Daoud s’est exprimée à la même occasion sur les positions controversées de l’écrivain, qu'elle dit clairement ne pas partager. « La voix de Kamel Daoud ne doit pas effacer la mienne », écrit-elle, assurant qu'elle « ne partage pas » ses positions sur « trois questions essentielles, l'Algérie, l'islam et la Palestine ». « Plus profondément encore, ce qui nous sépare, c'est le regard porté sur la douleur d'autrui », a écrit Aicha Dahdouh à propos de son époux. Kamel Daoud a toujours soutenu que sa femme est hors de cause dans cette affaire. L’article Affaire Kamel Daoud : sa femme sort du silence est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: ‘You need people, not money’ – Expert urges young people to explore agribusiness
items.description: Young people and aspiring entrepreneurs should not wait until they have substantial start-up capital before exploring opportunities in agribusiness, an agricultural development expert has said, urging them to identify market needs and build relationships that can help turn ideas into viable businesses. Executive Director of the Centre for Climate Change & Food Security (CCCFS) and Director of WAJESHA, Engr Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen, says he has trained, advised and guided nearly 300 people in 2026 alone to consider opportunities in the agricultural sector. The group includes students, graduates, businesspeople, politicians and teachers, whom he has reached through workshops, seminars, webinars, farm field visits, meetings and informal conversations, including on buses. “Sometimes, you don’t need money at the first point; you need people,” he told participants at an Agribusiness Incubation Workshop organised by residents of Jacob Jonas Nortey Hall at Valley View University’s Oyibi campus on Friday, 23 October 2026. Held under the theme “Developing the Anti-Fragile Mindset: Agribusiness as a Catalyst,” the workshop explored how young people could approach agriculture as a business and identify opportunities across its value chain. Identify a problem before investing Mohammed-Nurudeen said aspiring entrepreneurs should begin by identifying a problem they can solve rather than pursuing immediate profits without a clear understanding of the market. “If you really want to go into agribusiness, first problem identification. What problem do you want to address?” he asked. He illustrated the point with the story of a woman whose business collapsed during the COVID-19 pandemic but who found another source of income through the sale of locally produced rice. According to him, she identified people who needed rice, sourced the product from producers and supplied it to customers at a price that allowed her to make a profit. “Her business actually collapsed during the COVID-19, and she decided to solve that problem for people,” he said. The example, he explained, demonstrates how recognising an unmet need can help people identify business opportunities even when their original plans have failed. He also recounted how he advised a vegetable farmer who was struggling to find customers to prepare flyers and distribute them at ministries, where workers might have limited time to visit markets. Mohammed-Nurudeen said he encouraged the farmer to offer potential customers samples of the vegetables. “When he did that, the first week, second week, they started calling him for orders,” he said, describing the approach as an opportunity that opened the door to new customers. The experience highlights the importance of understanding customers and actively promoting products instead of relying on production alone to generate sales. ‘Networking first before money’ For Mohammed-Nurudeen, relationships can help aspiring entrepreneurs find customers, obtain advice and identify potential partners before they have the resources to establish a business. He drew on his experience travelling to nearly 2,500 communities across Ghana’s 16 regions, saying the relationships he had built over the years continued to provide access to people who could help him solve problems. “I’ve travelled to many communities and at least I have friends in each of the districts that I went to,” he said. He explained that he could contact people in those communities when he needed assistance, while relationships beyond Ghana had also helped him access professional opportunities. He cited invitations to contribute to international work involving climate change and health as examples of how professional networks and recommendations could open doors. “You might even have the money and you might even establish your business, but the business will collapse because you don’t have that strong network system,” he cautioned. He urged young people, particularly those below 25, to start building relationships early and not to measure every interaction by immediate financial returns. “There are things you need to do for free and these things can bring a lot of benefits to you,” he said. He also advised aspiring entrepreneurs to think carefully about what would distinguish their products from those of competitors. “If you want to go into maize cultivation, there are a lot of maize farmers. What unique thing are you bringing on board that you would want people to buy your maize?” he asked. Agribusiness goes beyond farming Mohammed-Nurudeen said entering agribusiness does not necessarily mean cultivating crops or rearing animals. Opportunities also exist in processing, marketing, distribution and other activities that connect agricultural products to consumers. “Setting up a business does not necessarily mean that you have to go and grow a crop,” he said. “You don’t necessarily have to go into farming physically.” He added: “The value chain is very long; you can choose any of them.” The advice encourages aspiring entrepreneurs to consider how their existing skills, resources and interests could fit into different parts of the agricultural sector rather than assuming that land ownership or direct involvement in production is essential. He also urged businesses to diversify so they could better withstand market disruptions and competition. Using the example of a business facing new competitors offering better products or services, he asked what an entrepreneur should do when customers begin moving elsewhere. “That is why we have always told farmers that they need to diversify,” he said. Diversification, he explained, can create additional income streams and reduce the risks associated with depending on a single product or business activity. Persistence is not enough Mohammed-Nurudeen challenged the idea that patience and persistence alone will guarantee business success, arguing that entrepreneurs must be willing to reassess their decisions when results do not improve. “Many instances you can be patient for 20 years, 30 years, it won’t work,” he said. “How do you persist when you are doing the wrong thing?” He urged aspiring entrepreneurs to use their time productively, evaluate what is happening in their businesses and adjust their approaches instead of continuing with strategies that are not working. Integrity, he added, is equally important to building a sustainable livelihood. Recounting a conversation with a retired public servant he met during a journey from Kumasi to Kintampo, Mohammed-Nurudeen said the man reflected on how he had previously withheld part of money intended for colleagues while working in public service. The man later decided to stop the practice and share a contract payment among his team members, according to Mohammed-Nurudeen’s account. The story reinforced the advice the retired public servant had given during their roadside conversation: “Money is good, but don’t be eager to make money by any means.” For Mohammed-Nurudeen, trust and sound judgement are as important as identifying a market opportunity. A business idea may create an opening, but sustaining it requires the ability to adapt, maintain relationships and act with integrity. A university initiative to expand agribusiness The workshop forms part of efforts by residents of Jacob Jonas Nortey Hall to develop and expand their agribusiness activities. The hall has previously undertaken a yam farming project and more recently ventured into mushroom production, with plans to diversify and scale up its initiatives. For students, graduates and others considering the sector, Mohammed-Nurudeen’s message was that a lack of substantial capital need not prevent them from exploring possibilities. Identifying a genuine need, finding ways to reach customers and building relationships can provide a starting point. The challenge, he suggested, is not simply to enter agriculture, but to identify where value can be created and remain ready to change course when circumstances demand it.

items.title: Open letter to President Mahama, Vice President Opoku-Agyemang and NDC leadership: Justice for Obuasi SHTS girls
items.description: Dear Mr President, Madam Vice President and leaders of the NDC, I write to you not as an adversary, but as a citizen who once believed that the phrase “social democratic” meant something more than a campaign slogan. I write because the events of the past week have made it impossible to remain silent. The sexual misconduct allegations against the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School involving 19 female students are not merely a criminal matter. They are a moral test of your government. And thus far, the response has been lackadaisical, reactive and, in the case of the Vice President, disturbingly belated. When investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, exposed the allegations, the party’s Functional Executive Committee first directed the accused, Zakaria Abdulai, to step aside from the Juaben constituency chairmanship race. Then, within days, the party reversed itself and cleared him to contest, citing the “presumption of innocence” and “the timelines of the ongoing electoral process”. It was only after public outrage that the party suspended its Amasaman Communications Officer, Daniel Nortey, for trivialising rape on live television. This is not principled leadership. It is crisis management. The signal sent to every girl in Obuasi and to every survivor of sexual violence in Ghana is unmistakable: when political convenience collides with your dignity, convenience wins. The signal being sent is that victims who are suffering may be discouraged from speaking up by what is happening today. Madam Vice President, you are the first woman to hold your office. That is a historic achievement, and it is not lost on the women of this country. But history is not a shield from accountability. Some organisations argue that you are “the Vice President of Ghana and not just the Vice President for women and girls”. They insist that your gender should not confine your leadership to women’s issues and that criticism of you is disproportionate. They are right about one thing: no woman should be reduced to her gender. But they are dangerously wrong about the political reality that put you in office. Madam Vice President, you did not win the sympathy of women voters by accident. You won it because your presence on the ticket promised representation; a promise that the highest office in the land would finally feel the weight of women’s lived realities. Women voted for you not because they expected you to be a “women’s officer”, but because they believed your gender would inform your judgement on issues that disproportionately affect them, such as rape, domestic violence, child defilement and the everyday indignities that too often go unspoken. To now position yourself as a neutral national leader, above the fray of gender, is to betray that promise. You cannot collect the political capital of women’s sympathy and then claim neutrality when women’s bodies are the battlefield. The argument by some organisations that you are “Vice President of Ghana, not for women” is technically true and politically dishonest. It is a sophisticated way of saying that the first woman in your position will be judged by the same standards as the men who preceded her, which is precisely the problem because those standards have failed women for generations. Mr President, your party’s response to Obuasi reveals a deeper disorder: the belief that the only real accountability is electoral. Polls and public commentary are treated as noise to be managed until the next vote. But elections are not a licence to govern without scrutiny. They are a mechanism for accountability, and that is only one of many. Public outrage, the media’s questions and the protests of civil society are not obstacles to your mandate. They are the tools by which a democracy checks power between elections. Until Ghanaians go to the polls again, public commentary is one of the checks on your government’s conscience. And that conscience, on Obuasi, has been found wanting. It is my humble appeal, Mr President, that you direct the Criminal Investigations Department to expedite its probe and ensure that no political consideration interferes with justice for the 19 girls of Obuasi SHTS in the alleged rape cases. I humbly appeal again to Madam Vice President, Her Excellency Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, to break your silence, not with another call for “due process”, but with a clear, unequivocal condemnation of sexual violence and a concrete commitment to survivor support. Use your office to convene, to demand and to protect. That is not the work of a “Vice President for Women”. It is the work of a Vice President for Ghana. And I call on the NDC to remember that, with so much happening in the last month, I believe it is too early to be comfortable. You made a promise to the vulnerable. Please, do not trade their pain for political advantage. The girls of Obuasi are watching. So are the women who voted for you. So is history. Long live the President and the Vice President, and long live Ghana. Yours in citizenship, Rebecca Abafum Former Organising Secretary, Ghana Association of Writers

items.title: ‘Some cannot afford to come home’ – Evacuees’ leader urges continued repatriation
items.description: The leader of the Aggrieved South Africa Evacuees, Michael Addo, has called for continued government support in repatriating Ghanaians stranded abroad, stressing that many citizens in South Africa and other countries are desperate to return home. According to him, several Ghanaians remain stranded overseas, with some unable to finance their return journeys despite their willingness to come back to Ghana. “We should rather encourage the government to continue with the repatriation because we still have individuals who are stranded not only in South Africa but in other countries who are willing to come home,” he stated. His appeal comes amid public scrutiny of the government’s reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa. Mr Addo explained that the desire of stranded Ghanaians to return home is not motivated by the financial reintegration packages offered to returnees, but by the hardships they continue to endure abroad. “Not because of the reintegration package, but because they are tired. Some do not even have the funds to come home,” he emphasised. He maintained that the ongoing controversy surrounding the evacuation exercise should not discourage the government from extending assistance to other vulnerable Ghanaians seeking to return. Mr Addo consequently urged the public to support further repatriation efforts, stressing the importance of prioritising the welfare of stranded citizens while discussions over the cost of the exercise continue.

items.title: Arabie saoudite : plus de 520 organismes attendus au Salon du Hajj à Djeddah
items.description: La ville saoudienne de Djeddah accueillera, du 8 au 11 novembre 2026, la sixième édition de la Conférence et du Salon du Hajj. Plus de 520 organismes issus des secteurs public, privé et à but non lucratif, ainsi que des représentants de plus de 150 pays, sont attendus à ce rendez-vous consacré à la préparation de la saison du Hajj 1448 de l’hégire, selon l’Agence de presse saoudienne (SPA). Organisé par le ministère saoudien du Hajj et de la Omra, en collaboration avec le Programme de service aux pèlerins, l’événement s’inscrit dans le cadre de la Vision saoudienne 2030. Il vise notamment à renforcer la coordination entre les acteurs du pèlerinage et à améliorer la qualité des services proposés aux pèlerins. Le salon s’étendra sur une superficie de plus de 67 000 m². Il réunira des prestataires intervenant dans plusieurs domaines, notamment le transport, la logistique, l’hébergement, la restauration, la santé, la sécurité, les infrastructures, les médias et les nouvelles technologies. Cette plateforme permettra également de présenter des solutions innovantes, de conclure des contrats et de nouer des partenariats destinés à optimiser les prestations offertes aux pèlerins. Plus de 15 espaces et programmes au menu Cette sixième édition proposera plus de 15 espaces et programmes, dont la Conférence du Hajj, des ateliers, un espace dédié à l’entrepreneuriat et à l’innovation, un hackathon et un centre d’affaires. Un Forum de sensibilisation et de formation sera organisé pour la première fois. Des espaces spécialisés seront également consacrés à la technologie, à la santé, aux médias et à l’aviation. Les travaux s’articuleront autour de trois axes principaux : les infrastructures et les services opérationnels, l’autonomisation et l’intégration, ainsi que le développement et la durabilité. Une rencontre réunira, par ailleurs, les responsables des bureaux chargés des affaires du Hajj. Les autorités saoudiennes entendent consolider ainsi les préparatifs de la prochaine saison du pèlerinage et renforcer l’efficacité des opérations, conformément aux objectifs du Programme de service aux pèlerins et de la Vision 2030. items.title: Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
items.description: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shit house country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shit house country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient of the prize. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. items.title: GPHA celebrates industry excellence at 40th Anniversary Awards Night
items.description: The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) has honoured outstanding customers, stakeholders and individuals for their contributions to the growth of Ghana’s maritime industry at a special Industry Awards Dinner held on Friday 23rd October, 2026 as part of activities marking the Authority’s 40th Anniversary celebration. Delivering the keynote address, the Minister for Transport Hon. Joseph Bukari Nikpe commended GPHA, its past and present leadership, staff and industry stakeholders for their collective role in transforming Ghana’s ports over the past four decades. He described the anniversary as a celebration of institutional growth, visionary leadership and enduring partnerships that have strengthened Ghana’s position in regional and international trade. Hon. Nikpe noted that Ghana’s ports remain strategic national assets that facilitate trade, create employment and support economic growth. He stressed the need for continuous improvements in port efficiency, digitalisation, multimodal connectivity, sustainability, workforce development and regional integration to position Ghana as the preferred logistics gateway for West Africa. According to him, achieving these objectives will require stronger collaboration among government, GPHA, private sector operators, customers and all stakeholders within the transport and logistics value chain. He urged industry players to sustain the spirit of partnership that has underpinned the Authority’s success over the years. The Chairman of the GPHA Board of Directors of GPHA, Johnson Asiedu Nketiah in his remarks, said the awards ceremony provided an opportunity to celebrate the individuals and institutions whose commitment, professionalism and partnership have contributed significantly to the Authority’s development and the growth of Ghana’s maritime sector. He acknowledged the critical role played by shipping lines, terminal operators, freight forwarders, transport operators, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders in supporting the Authority’s mission over the past 40 years. He reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to providing strategic direction and oversight to ensure that GPHA remains competitive and responsive to the evolving demands of global trade. Earlier, welcoming guests to the dinner, Director-General of GPHA, Major-General Paul Seidu Tanye-Kulono, described the Authority’s 40-year journey as a testament to the vision of its leaders, the dedication of employees and the confidence of stakeholders whose support has shaped the institution’s success. He noted that the growth of the ports has been driven by collaboration across the maritime and logistics value chain and expressed appreciation to stakeholders for their continued partnership and confidence in the Authority. Major-General Tanye-Kulono urged all stakeholders to build on the legacy of the past four decades by embracing innovation, strengthening partnerships and pursuing greater efficiency to ensure a stronger and more competitive port sector in the years ahead. The event brought together government officials, former Directors-General, members of the GPHA Board, management and staff, industry partners and customers to celebrate four decades of service, partnership and progress while recognising excellence across the maritime and logistics industry.

items.title: “I’ll always defend my colleagues” – Ablakwa says over S.A. evacuation allegation
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has defended the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its finance officers against allegations of financial irregularities in the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. Speaking at a press conference on Monday, October 26, organised by some of the evacuees, Mr Ablakwa said he would continue to defend his reputation, the ministry and the officials responsible for managing the funds. He insisted that no money had been misappropriated, despite media reports and allegations by the Minority in parliament regarding the disbursement of funds for the exercise. Although he acknowledged that he did not personally distribute the reported GH¢5,500 to every evacuee, the minister expressed confidence in the work of the ministry’s finance officers, maintaining that they had performed their duties diligently. “Now, I will always defend my colleagues at the foreign ministry, even though I did not personally hand over these funds, but I know that the team at the finance directorate of my ministry, the NADMO team, the National Security team, these are all public servants of impeccable integrity and nobody will seek to take advantage of traumatised evacuees from another country,” he said. The press conference comes amid growing scrutiny of the government’s expenditure on the evacuation exercise, following media fact-checks and claims by the Minority that not every evacuee received the reported GH¢5,500. Questions have also been raised about discrepancies in the dates of birth recorded in some of the documents provided by the ministry, further intensifying calls for clarification on the payments and the documentation process. The controversy centres on the transparency and accountability of the funds used to evacuate Ghanaians from South Africa, as well as the support reportedly provided to those who returned home. Mr Ablakwa’s defence is the latest development in the ongoing debate over the management of the exercise, with questions about the payments and supporting records remaining central to the public discussion.

items.title: Lutte contre la migration irrégulière : 28 personnes déférées au parquet
items.description: La Division nationale de lutte contre le trafic de migrants et pratiques assimilées (DNLT) a conduit 28 individus devant le parquet à l’issue d’une série d’opérations menées sur le territoire national. Les mis en cause sont poursuivis pour diverses infractions, notamment le trafic de migrants par voie maritime, la mise en danger de la vie d’autrui et l’escroquerie. Neuf affaires distinctes sont à l’origine de ces déferrements, selon les informations communiquées par les services de lutte contre le trafic de migrants. À Saint-Louis, plusieurs interventions ont permis de déférer des suspects poursuivis notamment pour association de malfaiteurs, trafic de migrants par voie maritime, tentative de trafic de migrants et complicité. Les opérations réalisées les 19 et 22 octobre 2026 ont respectivement conduit au déferrement de trois et deux individus dans les premières affaires, ainsi que de quatre autres personnes dans une affaire distincte. D’autres interventions menées par la DNLT ont abouti au déferrement de six individus pour association de malfaiteurs, tentative de trafic de migrants par voie maritime, mise en danger de la vie d’autrui et complicité. Cinq autres personnes sont poursuivies pour des faits similaires. Dans une autre affaire, quatre individus ont été déférés pour association de malfaiteurs, tentative de trafic de migrants par voie maritime, escroquerie et complicité. À Saint-Louis, trois personnes sont également poursuivies pour des faits présumés de tentative de trafic de migrants, d’escroquerie et d’infractions liées au chanvre indien, notamment son usage, sa détention et son trafic. À Karang, un individu a été déféré pour tentative de trafic de migrants par voie maritime, escroquerie et complicité. Une autre personne a également été présentée au parquet à Saint-Louis dans le cadre d’une affaire distincte. Les investigations se poursuivent afin de démanteler les réseaux impliqués dans le trafic de migrants et de lutter contre les filières de migration irrégulière.

items.title: Clarifications sur la cession du gisement pétrolier El Menzah à Exxoil
items.description: Khaled Bettine, PDG de la Société nationale de la distribution des pétroles (SNDP-Agil), a apporté, dans une publication sur son compte Facebook , des précisions concernant les informations circulant au sujet de la cession, par l’État, du gisement pétrolier d’El Menzah dans le golfe de Hammamet. Il s’agit, en réalité, de la régularisation d’une situation juridique et administrative en suspens depuis 2001, a-t-il indiqué, en précisant que ce gisement a été découvert en 1998 et est entré en phase de production en 2000. L’exploitation a cessé en 2007, suite à une baisse de la production tombée à environ 35 barils par jour ; la production totale cumulée, sur toute la période d’exploitation, s’est élevée à près de 1,9 million de barils, a-t-il ajouté, en soulignant que l’Entreprise tunisienne d’activités pétrolières (Etap) avait décidé, en 2001, de ne pas participer au développement et à la production du gisement. Toutefois, la décision d’octroi de la concession d’exploitation, émise en novembre 2000, n’a pas été mise à jour en temps opportun, ce qui a maintenu la situation juridique dans un état nécessitant une régularisation. En 2024, la société Exxoil a déposé une demande de modification de la décision d’octroi de la concession, suite à la faillite de la société Ecumed Petroleum Grombalia en 2021. Selon les informations relatives au dossier, le Comité consultatif des hydrocarbures, l’instance publique chargée de donner des avis obligatoires et conformes ou consultatifs au ministre de l’Energie sur les questions relatives aux titres miniers (permis de recherche, concessions d’exploitation), a approuvé, en septembre 2024, le transfert des droits et obligations de la société en faillite à Exxoil (Groupe Setcar). Bettine a par ailleurs souligné que l’entreprise en question envisage de mener de nouvelles opérations d’exploration, des estimations suggérant que le gisement pourrait receler des ressources pétrolières encore non découvertes. Rappelons que la cession de la concession d’exploitation du gisement d’El Menzah à la société Exxoil a suscité une vive controverse. Le député Imed Ouled Jibril a notamment exigé des clarifications officielles concernant la nature des droits cédés, leur valeur financière, ainsi que la contrepartie — le cas échéant — perçue par l’Etap. Il a également interrogé les autorités sur les revenus attendus pour l’État, ainsi que sur les engagements de la société en matière d’investissements et de protection de l’environnement. Par ailleurs, le député a appelé à la publication des accords, des études d’évaluation et des documents afférents à cette décision, et a réclamé que l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) puisse y avoir accès afin d’exercer sa mission de contrôle, en insistant, en outre, sur la nécessité de garantir la transparence, de préserver les droits de l’État et de défendre l’intérêt national. Les clarifications de M. Bettine sont certes les bienvenues, mais la polémique à ce sujet aurait pu être évitée si l’État avait fait preuve de davantage de transparence et de moins de cachotteries d’un autre âge. S’agissant de ressources nationales, les Tunisiens sont en droit de tout savoir sur les tenants et les aboutissants de toute opération à caractère économique et commercial engageant la responsabilité de l’État. I. B. L’article Clarifications sur la cession du gisement pétrolier El Menzah à Exxoil est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Central bank raises policy rate by 50 basis points to 12pc
items.description: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday raised the key policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 per cent, its first increase since April as inflation, fuelled by high energy costs due to the Gulf conflict, remained above target. In a statement, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) said it had decided to increase the policy rate, with a majority decision of nine out of ten members. It noted that the “intensification in the Middle East conflict and low prospects of its near-term resolution” were keeping global energy prices at persistently elevated levels. “While the impact of this global shock on the domestic economy has remained contained so far amidst proactive monetary policy adjustment and continued fiscal discipline, geopolitical developments have worsened the inflation outlook as compared to the earlier assessment,” it said. It went on to say that although the external account and growth outlook remained broadly unchanged, risks had also increased. “Considering these developments and the evolving risks, the MPC deemed today’s decision as necessary to keep inflation expectations anchored, contain second-round effects of the ongoing supply shock and bring inflation within the target range of 5-7pc. This will help preserve macroeconomic stability, which is necessary for sustainable economic growth,” it said. It said that forex reserves had remained stable at around $21bn, Pakistan had reached a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and that real gross domestic product (GDP) growth had been revised at 3.7pc, almost unchanged from the initial estimate. It further said that the Federal Board of Revenue had exceeded its revenue collection target during the first quarter of the current fiscal year, major central banks had raised interest rates in the wake of rising inflationary pressures and the IMF had also revised its global inflation projections upwards. “While noting these developments and the increasing frequency of global supply shocks, the MPC emphasized the importance of increasing external and fiscal buffers to further strengthen the economy’s resilience. The committee also reiterated that continuing the prudent monetary and fiscal policy mix, alongside timely implementation of structural reforms, is essential for achieving higher and sustainable economic growth,” the statement said. Regarding inflation, which eased to 10.3pc in September from 11pc in Augus, the MPC said that the re-escalation in the Middle East conflict and domestic wheat supply frictions were two major factors keeping inflation at elevated levels It said that their expected continuation over the next few months had “worsened the inflation outlook”. It added that there was a risk that elevated food and energy inflation may further increase inflation expectations, which may seep into core inflation going forward. “In view of these developments and increasing risks to the inflation outlook, the committee assessed today’s decision as important to keep the real policy rate adequately positive on forward-looking basis. This is necessary to bring inflation within the target range over the medium term. The inflation outlook is subject to multiple risks, including geopolitical tensions, global commodity price volatility, unanticipated adjustments in energy tariffs, further uptick in wheat and allied product prices and adverse weather conditions,” it said. Regarding the external sector, the statement said that exports were recovering, adding that remittances had remained resilient and were projected to turn out higher than the earlier assessment. It said that the current account deficit in FY27 was assessed to remain within the earlier projected range of 0-1pc of GDP. “This, along with higher financial inflows, is expected to increase SBP’s FX reserves beyond the current level. This outlook, however, remains susceptible to multiple risks, including elevated global commodity prices, tightening international financial conditions, and supply constraints,” it said. As per the statement, the committee expected GDP growth to remain within previously projected ranges of 3.5pc to 4.5pc in FY27. However, it added that the outlook was susceptible to risks from escalation in the Middle East conflict and adverse climate events such as El Niño conditions. SBP governor cites inflationary outlook SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed also addressed a press conference to announce the decision and said there were many “underlying factors” behind the decision, especially the inflation outlook. He cited the US-Israel war on Iran and its impact on energy and oil prices, developments in the domestic market and the subsequent impact on inflation. He said that nine out of ten MPC members voted to raise the policy rate, while one member had a different view; they were of the opinion that it should be raised further. He said that consumer expectations and other forecasters’ views were taken into consideration, as well as other macro factors, especially the impact of global commodity and oil prices on the external account and the impact of remittances and export trends. Ahmed noted a deterioration in the current account since the last MPC meeting. However, he added: “The good thing is that its impact is still between zero and one per cent of GDP and it will stay between that.” He also shared that the central bank revised its outlook on remittances, from $44 billion to $45bn. On exports, the SBP governor said the trend was witnessing an improvement; however, it was not yet in line with the economy’s needs. He added that the bank estimated imports to be close to $71bn. He said it would take longer than planned for inflation to get within the target range and revised GDP growth to 3.7pc for the current fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. Meanwhile, Topline Securities said the central bank had raised the policy rate “in line with our expectations”. Previously, the policy rate was 11.5pc. The central bank had held the rate steady since raising it by 100 basis points in April in response to rising global energy prices and supply chain risks — its first increase in nearly three years. The SBP has cut the key rate by a cumulative 1,050 basis points since mid-2024 , from a record 22pc reached in June 2023, as inflation cooled sharply from multi-decade highs. Last week, the IMF called for Pakistan’s fiscal policy to go beyond achieving primary balance targets and protecting debt sustainability by reinforcing policy credibility, fostering economic recovery and creating space for public investment and social spending to support stronger long-term growth. Additional input from Reuters
